item.title: PM calls Awami League a ‘terrorist group’, urges democratic unity
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday described the ousted Awami League as a “terrorist group” and urged all democratic political forces to unite against what he called attempts by the party and its fugitive leaders to destabilise Bangladesh.
Speaking at the concluding sitting of the fourth session of the 13th National Parliament, he said democratic parties, both inside and outside the house, should stand together as they did during the 2024 uprising to prevent the return of what he termed defeated authoritarian forces.
Referring to recent violence in Gopalganj’s Tungipara and elsewhere, Tarique accused the Awami League of acting as a terrorist organisation rather than a political party. He also alleged that its fugitive leaders had urged supporters to set fire to homes and prepare lists of people to be killed.
The prime minister criticised a neighbouring country for allegedly sheltering and supporting fugitive Awami League leaders and using them to destabilise Bangladesh. He said the country's people would not accept subservience to any foreign power.
Tarique also alleged that attempts to create unrest in the garment sector were part of a conspiracy by ousted Awami League forces against the democratic government.
He said the government was aware of workers’ concerns and was discussing the issues with all stakeholders. He expressed hope that the Minimum Wages Board would announce a new minimum wage soon.
Urging workers not to be provoked into damaging factories, he said the garment industry had been built through decades of joint efforts by workers and entrepreneurs.
“If you destroy the factory, where will your salary come from? How will you get paid?” he asked, appealing to workers to protect their workplaces and livelihoods.
The prime minister also referred to alleged harassment of former interim government Chief Adviser Prof Muhammad Yunus in the United States, NCP Convener Nahid Islam in the United Kingdom and an attack on a Bangladeshi cultural artiste in Italy.
Tarique praised lawmakers from the treasury and opposition benches for their participation in the parliamentary session and outlined several government initiatives, including the Family Card, Farmers’ Card, Health Card and Notun Kuri Sports programme.
The speaker prorogued the fourth session at 6:39pm after completing the question-and-answer session and legislative business.

item.title: Former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid detained in Uttara
item.description:
Former education minister and Awami League advisory council member Nurul Islam Nahid was detained by police from a residence in the capital's Uttara area early Thursday in connection with cases filed over killings during the 2024 student-led uprising.
Police took him into custody around 2:20am during a raid on a house on Road 2 in Sector 3, where he had been living with his family.
Uttara West Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Khalid Mansur confirmed the detention, saying Nahid had been taken to the police station.
The police official said multiple cases had been filed against the former minister over killings during the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.
Police were examining the allegations and the next legal steps, he added.
Nahid is a senior leader of the activities-banned Awami League and a former lawmaker from the Sylhet-6 constituency, comprising Beanibazar and Golapganj.
He served as education minister for a decade after the Awami League formed the government following the 2008 parliamentary election.

item.title: Four killed as violence, arson spread ahead of Awami League lockdown
item.description:
At least four people have been killed in separate incidents of political violence and arson in Bangladesh over two days as clashes, crude bomb attacks and widespread destruction intensified ahead of the activities-banned Awami League’s nationwide lockdown on Thursday.
Two BNP-affiliated leaders were killed in Narail on Wednesday evening in an attack allegedly carried out by Awami League activists, while a Krishak Dal leader died in Faridpur on Tuesday night.
A bus helper was also burnt alive in Pirojpur early Wednesday when unidentified assailants torched two parked buses.
The violence extended from Gopalganj, where a police station, security vehicles and BNP lawmakers’ residences were attacked, to several other districts, prompting the deployment of hundreds of additional security personnel.
In Narail’s Kalia upazila, Krishak Dal leader Shahinur Sheikh, 45, and Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (Jasas) leader Sohel Molla, 35, were killed when attackers assaulted a motorcycle procession organised by BNP-affiliated groups to protest Awami League-linked violence.
The attack occurred at Bottola intersection in Bendar Char on Wednesday evening. Narail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Al Mamun Shikder confirmed the two deaths around 10pm. Several others were injured.
In Faridpur’s Bhanga, Krishak Dal leader Raju Molla died after suffering severe burns during a blockade on the Dhaka-Barishal highway on Tuesday night.
BNP leaders accused Awami League and Chhatra League activists of attacking him and torching motorcycles. Police said efforts were underway to identify those responsible.
In Pirojpur’s Bhandaria, bus helper Mohammad Siam was burnt to death while sleeping inside a parked bus after unidentified attackers set fire to two vehicles around 3:45am Wednesday. Police said the perpetrators had not been identified.
Several shops were also torched in Nazirpur, where attackers targeted a union parishad warehouse containing government-subsidised food supplies.
Gopalganj remained a major flashpoint following Tuesday night’s attacks on Tungipara Police Station, police and Border Guard Bangladesh vehicles, and at least 20 houses, including the residence of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani.
Vehicles are set on fire and barricades are created at several locations along the Dhaka-Khulna highway in Kashiani upazila, including Tarail, Gopalpur, Fokra, Tilchhara and Ghonapara, on Wednesday evening ahead of the November 19 lockdown. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
The violence erupted after police arrested several suspected Awami League and Chhatra League activists. Protesters subsequently stormed the station, vandalised the premises and set vehicles ablaze.
By Wednesday evening, most personnel had reportedly moved from Tungipara Police Station to the district police lines amid fears of renewed attacks. Authorities deployed 21 BGB platoons across Gopalganj to restore security.
In another attack around 8pm Wednesday, unidentified assailants set fire to the front gate of Gopalganj-2 MP Dr KM Babar’s residence and vandalised his personal office.
Patients, including newborns and women recovering from Caesarean sections, fled a clinic housed in the same building. No casualties were reported.
The escalating unrest also disrupted education in Gopalganj, where the local science and technology university announced a two-day closure and postponed examinations. Security was reinforced around the district jail.
Elsewhere, two police officers were injured in Cox’s Bazar’s Ramu when relatives of a Swechchhasebak League leader allegedly attacked police and freed him from custody.
In Khulna, unidentified attackers hurled a crude bomb into the district judge’s court building on Wednesday night, although it failed to explode.
In Rangpur, two buses were set ablaze within 10 hours, with detectives suspecting Chhatra League involvement. The attacks disrupted transport services and spread panic among residents.
Retaliatory violence was also reported against Awami League properties.
In Sirajganj, attackers set fire to the party’s district office and the residence of former lawmaker Habibe Millat Munna.
In Cumilla, the Awami League office and former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar’s residence were attacked and set ablaze.
Meanwhile, crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson have been reported across at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, according to police figures cited by Reuters. At least 37 Grameen Bank offices have also been targeted since November 10.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of encouraging violence and warned that those responsible for attacks and sabotage would face prosecution.
The violence has heightened fears of further confrontation as the Awami League prepares to enforce its today’s lockdown, while Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal has announced a procession in Dhaka on Thursday.

item.title: Two BNP leaders killed in attack on rally in Narail
item.description:
Two BNP leaders were killed after activists of the activities-banned Awami League allegedly attacked a BNP procession in Kalia Upazila of Narail on Wednesday evening.
The attack took place around 7pm during a procession organised to protest terrorism and lawlessness.
The deceased were Shahin, general secretary of Kalia Upazila Krishak Dal, and Sohel Molla, general secretary of the upazila unit of Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sangskritik Sangstha (JASAS).
Police and local sources said BNP and its affiliated organisations brought out the procession in Kalia town. Awami League activists allegedly attacked the march, leaving Shahin and Sohel Molla critically injured.
They were taken to hospital, where doctors declared them dead.
Narail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Al Mamun Sikder confirmed the deaths to Bangla Tribune around 10pm.

item.title: Actress Jyotika Jyoti arrested in Uttara
item.description:
Actress Jyotika Jyoti, whose name previously surfaced in a controversial WhatsApp group linked to supporters of the ousted Awami League government, was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police in the capital’s Uttara area early Thursday.
A DB team arrested her around 2:45am from a government residential quarter in Sector 18, under Turag Police Station.
Ilias Kabir, acting deputy commissioner of the DB’s Uttara division, confirmed the arrest, saying the actress had been taken to the DB office.
However, police did not immediately disclose the charges against her or identify the case in which she was arrested.
Jyoti previously drew criticism after her name appeared among members of a WhatsApp group called “Alo Ashbei” (Light Will Come), whose conversations became public following the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024.
Screenshots circulated in September 2024 showed group members, including actors, journalists and cultural figures, making disparaging remarks about the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement and protesters.
Following the controversy, Jyoti addressed her involvement in a Facebook Live session, saying the group was not intended to harm the country or its people.
She maintained that she had only shared information about developments in Dhaka during the protests and said no artist could support the killing of people.

item.title: Dipu Moni, Sujit Roy Nandi’s homes torched
item.description:
Unidentified attackers set fire to the residences of former education minister Dr Dipu Moni and Awami League organising secretary Sujit Roy Nandi in separate incidents in Chandpur on Wednesday night.
The attacks, reported within half an hour of each other, targeted properties belonging to two senior figures of the activities-banned Awami League.
Around 9pm, attackers allegedly broke into Dipu Moni’s abandoned third-floor residence at Kadamtala Market in the town’s Notun Bazar area and set fire to the premises.
Residents of the building and neighbours extinguished the flames using water.
Advocate Gazi Dulal, who lives on the fifth floor, said the fire caused panic among residents.
He added that the apartment had already been extensively damaged in an arson attack on August 5, 2024, and that Wednesday’s fire mainly affected the remaining debris.
Chandpur Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Fayez Ahmed said he had not received information about the incident but would look into it.
Around 9:30pm, another group of attackers set fire to Sujit Roy Nandi’s two-storey house in Farakkabad village of Chandpur Sadar upazila.
Dipu, a member of Ward 7 of Balia Union Parishad, said the attackers arrived on 40–50 motorcycles before setting the house ablaze.
Local residents attempted to extinguish the flames, but the house was gutted.
Firefighters reached the scene around 11:15pm, by which time the fire had destroyed most of the property.
Chandpur Fire Service official Md Abdullah said most of the furniture had already been destroyed when firefighters arrived.

item.title: Dr Yunus’s ancestral house in Chittagong set on fire
item.description:
The ancestral house of former interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus was set on fire in Chittagong city around 11:30pm on Wednesday, amid incidents of sabotage allegedly involving leaders and activists of the banned Awami League across the country.
According to a report by Prothom Alo, the fire broke out in an abandoned room on the ground floor of the house in the city's Panchlaish area.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Panchlaish police station Mozammel Haque said police personnel were regularly patrolling the area when they noticed the fire and rushed to the spot. They later extinguished it.
Police are investigating who was involved in the incident, he said.
Responding to a question, Mozammel said nobody lives on the ground floor of the building, which remains abandoned. The families of Yunus's 2 brothers live on the second and third floors.
He added that security around the house had been strengthened following the incident.
A few days ago, miscreants set fire to 2 branches of Grameen Bank in Anwara and Satkania upazilas of Chittagong.
The main ancestral house of Grameen Bank founder Professor Yunus is located in Bathua village of Hathazari upazila in Chittagong. His father was a businessman, and through that connection, Yunus built the house in Panchlaish city.
Professor Yunus spent his childhood and adolescence in the Panchlaish house.

item.title: Crude bomb explosions at separate locations in capital, one detained
item.description:
Crude bomb explosions at separate locations in Dhaka on Wednesday evening left a woman seriously injured, while police detained one person in connection with twin explosions in Shyampur.
The incident in Shahjahanpur occurred on Wednesday, November 18, evening in front of Khilgaon Government Primary School, adjacent to Khilgaon Railgate Market, under Shahjahanpur police station.
Shahjahanpur police station Officer-in-Charge Amirul Islam said unidentified miscreants threw a crude bomb from atop the Khilgaon Flyover. It exploded on the road, seriously injuring nearby tea shop owner Nasima Begum, 40.
She was later admitted to Mugda Medical College Hospital.
Meanwhile, Shyampur police station Officer-in-Charge Md Nazrul Islam said twin crude bomb explosions occurred in front of the Dholai Par bus counter.
A person was caught red-handed at the time.

item.title: RMG unrest escalates, 300 arrested as clashes spread
item.description:
Garment workers’ protests demanding a Tk30,000 minimum monthly wage intensified across Dhaka, Gazipur, Savar and Ashulia on Wednesday, triggering fresh clashes with police, highway blockades and factory closures, while nearly 300 people have been arrested in connection with the continuing unrest.
The escalating confrontation, now in its third week, has disrupted production across Bangladesh’s largest export industry, with workers accusing authorities of delaying wage negotiations and police stepping up operations to contain the violence.
In Gazipur, thousands of workers blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway around 9am, bringing traffic to a standstill in Chhaydana, Hariken and surrounding industrial areas.
A vehicle belonging to Gazipur Metropolitan Police was set ablaze during clashes.
Police confirmed the arson, while law enforcement personnel worked to disperse protesters and restore traffic, which normalised after 2pm.
At least 20 factories in Savar and Ashulia remained closed amid the unrest, while several factories in Gazipur also suspended operations.
In Savar’s Ulail area, thousands of workers from Al-Muslim Group and nearby factories blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway around 2:30pm.
Clashes erupted when police attempted to clear the road. Officers fired tear gas and rubber bullets after protesters allegedly threw bricks, forcing workers to retreat around 4pm.
Similar confrontations occurred in Ashulia’s Narsinghapur area, where police used tear gas to disperse workers attempting to block the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. Several people, including police personnel, were injured.
In the capital, garment workers clashed with police in Pallabi and became involved in confrontations with local BNP activists in Kafrul following allegations that female workers had been harassed.
Police used sound grenades to restore order.
Police said nearly 300 people had been arrested in 24 cases filed with Savar and Ashulia police stations over alleged sabotage during the continuing protests.
Two leaders of the Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation were also arrested in Dhaka on Tuesday night on allegations of inciting unrest.
The unrest intensified after the minimum wage board postponed its third meeting, scheduled for November 16. The meeting has now been rescheduled for November 23.
Workers are demanding an increase in the minimum wage from Tk12,500 to Tk30,000, arguing that rising living costs have eroded their purchasing power.
Labour leaders say uncertainty over the wage board’s proceedings has fuelled mistrust among workers, who want the new wage structure announced before December and implemented from December 1.
Meanwhile, lawmakers from both treasury and opposition benches have expressed support for a reasonable wage increase while alleging that vested interests, including elements linked to the ousted Awami League, are attempting to exploit the unrest.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told the National Parliament that some groups were deliberately prolonging the protests despite ongoing negotiations between workers and factory owners.

item.title: One public toilet for every 1.72 lakh people in Dhaka
item.description:
Dhaka has just one public toilet for every 172,641 residents, exposing a severe sanitation crisis in the densely populated capital, where inadequate facilities, poor maintenance and user fees are forcing many people to relieve themselves in public spaces while women increasingly restrict their water intake to avoid using toilets outside their homes.
According to the United Nations’ World Urbanization Prospects 2025, Dhaka’s estimated population stands at 36.6 million.
Yet data from Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) show only 219 public toilets, including mobile facilities.
Of these, three have been demolished and four remain closed, leaving 212 in the existing network, some of which are also not operational.
This translates to approximately 0.58 public toilets per 100,000 residents, highlighting the scale of the shortage on the World Toilet Day.
In his message marking World Toilet Day 2026, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said sanitation was a universal human right, stressing that safe and accessible toilets were essential to protecting women’s health, safety and dignity.
He noted that inadequate sanitation exposes millions of women and girls to risks, discourages them from eating and drinking while outside their homes, and restricts their participation in education, employment and public life.
DNCC records show 131 public toilets, including 81 established by the city corporation and eight mobile facilities primarily used for special events rather than regular public access.
Another 42 are operated by organisations including WaterAid Bangladesh, SPACE, BhumiJ and ARBAN.
DSCC has 88 public toilets, one of which, beside Shaheed Zia Shishu Park, has been demolished.
Among the closed facilities are toilets at Golartek Field in Mirpur-1, Gabtoli Sluice Gate, Mirpur Section 13 Park and Avenue 8 in Mirpur-11.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/ Dhaka Tribune
Some have never opened despite completed construction, while others are undergoing renovation.
During visits to several public toilets, a Dhaka Tribune correspondent found missing soap and tissue paper, poor cleanliness and unpleasant smells.
Many facilities charged at least Tk10 per use.
The shortage is particularly difficult for an estimated two million drivers and transport workers who spend much of their working day on the streets.
During visits from Shewrapara through Farmgate to the University of Dhaka’s Teacher-Student Centre (TSC), the correspondent observed at least 30 people urinating beside roads and on footpaths.
Similar scenes were visible in Shahbagh, Kawran Bazar and Agargaon.
Sadman Hossain, a private-sector employee, described the situation near TSC as unbearable.
“I have to hold my breath while passing through this area. So many people are urinating openly on the footpaths, but there seems to be no one to look into it,” he said.
Another private-sector employee in Agargaon admitted urinating beside the road because he could not find a public toilet nearby.
Dhaka has an estimated 2 million rickshaw, van, CNG and other vehicle drivers and workers, many of whom spend most of their day on the streets.
The lack of affordable and accessible sanitation facilities particularly affects these groups.
For women, the shortage creates additional health, safety and dignity concerns.
Shahinur Begum said she deliberately reduces her water intake before leaving home to avoid needing a toilet.
“Once I am outside, I try not to drink water unless absolutely necessary because I might need to use a toilet,” she said.
Photo: Ahadul Karim Khan/ Dhaka Tribune
A WaterAid study, Women on the Go: How Poor Sanitation Influences Urban Women’s Water Intake in Bangladesh, found that 69% of women reduced their water consumption while outside, while another 15% avoided drinking water altogether.
Inspections at New Market, Mohakhali and Farmgate revealed broken door locks, unhygienic water containers, missing soap and tissue, and inadequate menstrual hygiene facilities.
At Mohakhali Inter-District Bus Terminal, several toilets previously designated for women have reportedly been converted into men’s facilities.
Ferdousi Begum, who travelled from Kishoreganj with her child, said she had no choice but to use an unhygienic toilet.
“It was not properly clean or suitable for use, but what else could I do?” she said.
Public health expert Dr Mushtuq Husain warned that inadequate sanitation increases the risk of infectious diseases and other health complications.
He said women who repeatedly delay urination may face urinary tract and bladder problems.
Urban planner Adil Mohammad Khan said public toilets should be treated as essential urban infrastructure, ideally available within every 400–500 metres.
He also questioned why residents must pay for such a basic necessity.
“People already pay taxes. Why should they have to pay for basic necessities?” he said.
DNCC Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton acknowledged that existing facilities were insufficient and said the corporation was working with WaterAid and other organisations to establish more toilets in high-demand areas.
“We recently held coordination meetings with WaterAid and other NGOs to discuss public toilets. We are working on establishing more facilities through a joint initiative involving the city corporation and WaterAid. We are prioritising areas with heavy public movement and where people face the greatest difficulties,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
DSCC Administrator Abdus Salam said the corporation was identifying locations for new toilets and strengthening monitoring of maintenance contractors.
“Thousands of people come to Dhaka every day from different parts of the country. We are trying to increase the number of public toilets and are already identifying locations where they are needed,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
“We are also taking steps to strengthen monitoring and address problems relating to cleanliness, maintenance and repairs,” he added.

item.title: Armed activists torch hospital, five BNP offices in Gopalganj
item.description:
Activists of the activities-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League staged armed demonstrations across Gopalganj town on Wednesday evening, attacking and setting fire to a private hospital. At least five BNP offices in the district were also torched during the day.
Witnesses said groups of activists carrying locally made weapons, including machetes and cleavers, rode motorcycles through Pachuria, the court area, Launch Ghat, Kachabazar intersection, Police Lines and Bedgram after 7:15pm.
The groups later gathered at Launch Ghat, where they chanted slogans under the leadership of Raju Khan, joint general secretary of the district Chhatra League.
Meanwhile, attackers led by Omar Faruk Khan Ripon, a former joint convener of the activities-banned organisation’s municipal unit, targeted Araf General Hospital and Diagnostic Centre, owned by Gopalganj-2 MP Dr KM Babar.
The attackers went live on Facebook as they vandalised the pathology unit, reception area and the lawmaker’s personal office on the ground floor of the five-storey building. They brought furniture outside, poured petrol on it and set it on fire. A crude bomb was also exploded during the attack.
Several patients, including pregnant women, women recovering from caesarean sections and newborns, were receiving treatment at the hospital. The attack triggered panic as relatives tried to move them to safety.
Separately, at least five BNP offices in different areas of Muksudpur Uupazila were set on fire between noon and evening. The Kashiani Upazila BNP Office and several union-level party offices were also attacked. Two Grameen Bank offices came under attack as well.
Earlier in the day, activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League staged demonstrations with machetes, Chinese axes and other locally made weapons at several points along the Gopalganj-Tungipara road. They also blocked six locations along the road by placing tree trunks and bamboo across it.

item.title: Crude bomb hurled at Khulna court building
item.description:
Miscreants threw a crude bomb at the ground floor of the Khulna District Judge Court building around 8:30pm on Wednesday, but it did not explode, causing no damage, police said.
Witnesses in the court area said two youths hurled the crude bomb before fleeing the scene. Police later visited the spot and recovered the unexploded device.
Khulna Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Lokman Hossain Ripon said that police recovered an unexploded crude bomb from the scene after receiving information.
“None could identify the attackers in the darkness. Efforts are underway to identify them,” he said.

item.title: Crude bomb hurled at Bogra Upazila Parishad premises
item.description:
A crude bomb was hurled at Bogra Sadar Upazila Parishad in the Matidali area of Bogra around 11pm on Tuesday.
Police and local sources said three men arrived on a motorcycle, with one of them throwing a crude bomb towards the upazila complex before the group sped away.
A 16-second video of the incident later circulated on social media, showing the attackers fleeing on their motorcycle while chanting “Joy Bangla”.
Bogra Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ibrahim Ali said the crude bomb was thrown from the road towards the complex, but did not explode inside the premises. Two Ansar members were on duty at the time but could not identify the attackers.
Police visited the scene and are working to identify those involved, he added.
Meanwhile, “Joy Bangla” slogans have been found written on government offices, officials’ residences, educational institutions, an eye hospital’s signboard and road dividers in Sherpur upazila of Bogra.
Sherpur Police Station OC Md Ekramul Hossain said an investigation was underway to identify those responsible for the graffiti.

Rifah Tasnia Swarna to lead Walton’s EV project
item.description:
Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC has appointed Rifah Tasnia Swarna, a successful entrepreneur, as monitoring director of its electric vehicle (EV) Project.
She is the youngest leader to take charge of the company’s most futuristic venture to date.
The decision was taken at Walton’s 69th Executive Committee (EC) meeting and confirmed in a letter from the managing director dated November 17.
The appointment aims to move the EV project forward in an organized, well-planned way as the company expands into new business areas.
For Swarna, this role is deeply personal.
The EV project was the dream of her late brother, Mahabub Alam Mridul (1997–2021), director of Walton Group.
He wanted Bangladesh to build its own electric vehicles, but he passed away before he could see that dream come true. Now his sister is taking it forward, giving his unfinished vision a new beginning.
In her new role, Swarna will oversee all work on the project and give the teams involved the guidance they need.
The board of directors said they were confident that her judgement, strong leadership and steady oversight would bring real progress in delivering the project.
Swarna is one of the country’s leading emerging business leaders.
She has already proven herself as a successful entrepreneur in several fields.
She is the founder of Savvata by Rifah, a luxury bridal and occasion wear label, director of Redmin Chemical Industries, and key founder of Kavva, a popular restaurant in Bashundhara R/A.
Leading the EV project puts her at the front of a future-focused industry, and she is set to help shape how Bangladesh moves in the years ahead.

item.title: Bangladesh Hopewell Hospitals (BHH) opens new diagnostic center in Bakalia, Chittagong
item.description:
Healthcare is one of the most fundamental needs of human life. Yet, for many underprivileged people, access to healthcare remains a significant challenge. For some, receiving essential medical care is still a distant dream.
With the aim of turning this dream into reality, the management of BSRM initiated plans to establish a charitable, welfare-oriented initiative dedicated to providing free healthcare services to underprivileged communities, operating under the umbrella of Bangladesh Hopewell Hospitals (BHH).
The objective of BHH is simple—to ensure that financial limitations do not prevent anyone from receiving essential medical care. BHH has already been providing healthcare services in Mirsarai and Chittagong.
Continuing this commitment, a new Diagnostic Center of Bangladesh Hopewell Hospitals has been formally inaugurated in Bakalia, Chittagong.
On Tuesday, Bangladesh Hopewell Hospitals (BHH) inaugurated its new Diagnostic Center in Bakalia, Chittagong, with the objective of expanding and improving access to essential healthcare services free of charge for underprivileged communities.
The inauguration ceremony was graced by Dr Mohammad Ziauddin, divisional commissioner, Chittagong, as chief guest.
Zahidul Islam Meah, deputy commissioner and district magistrate, Chittagong; Dr Shekh Fazle Rabbi, divisional director of health, Chittagong; and Dr Mohammad Sajedur Rahman, civil surgeon, Chittagong, attended the ceremony as special guests.
Also present at the event were Alihissain Akberali, chairman of BSRM Group; Zohaair Taherali, finance director; Abdul Qadir Zohair, director; and Tapan Sen Gupta, deputy managing director (DMD), along with other senior officials of BSRM Group and distinguished guests.
Located on the second floor of Green Leaf Tower, Bakalia Access Road, the new center covers an area of 3,988 square feet.
The center is expected to begin providing healthcare services to patients from November 21, 2026.
The center will offer medical consultations, prescribed medicines, diagnostic tests, and physiotherapy services.
Patients will receive medical consultations from BHH's Medical Officers, along with prescribed medicines and necessary diagnostic tests based on the recommendations of the attending physicians.
Physiotherapy services will also be available for patients requiring rehabilitative care.
For many financially disadvantaged individuals and families, the cost of medical treatment remains a major barrier to receiving timely healthcare.
By bringing these essential services together under one roof, BHH aims to ease this financial burden and help patients access the medical care they need.
This initiative reflects BSRM Group's continued commitment to social welfare and community wellbeing.
Through this effort, Bangladesh Hopewell Hospitals aims to make a meaningful contribution to improving access to healthcare services in Chittagong.

item.title: Honor launches 600S 5G in Bangladesh
item.description:
Honor has officially launched the Honor 600S 5G in Bangladesh at an event at Radisson Blu Dhaka.
The device seamlessly integrates AI-powered features with performance and durability.
Abdullah Al Mamun, head of business and Syed Md Badrul Arifeen, director and head of product and marketing, attended the event from Honor Bangladesh.
Special guests Toma Mirza and Keya Payel attended the celebration along with many lifestyle and technology content creators.
As part of the celebration, Honor unveiled its Brand Anthem created by Xefer, Masha and Ratul of Feroz Zong, along with its accompanying music video, which was brought to life using AI.
The three artists also delivered solo performances at the event.
Another highlight was the announcement of three winners of Honor’s AI Creator’s Den campaign, an initiative aimed at encouraging young creators to explore their creativity through AI.
Syed Md Badrul Arifeen said: “We believe technology should empower people to explore new possibilities, express their ideas and create something of their own. The AI Creator’s Den campaign reflects this belief by providing emerging talents with a platform to experiment with AI-powered content creation and showcase their ideas.”
The Honor 600S 5G combines intuitive AI functionalities with peak battery performance for everyday use.
A dedicated tactile AI button provides quick access to multiple AI features, including AI Image to Video 2.0, which allows users to generate and edit short videos through conversational commands.
Commenting on the smartphone, Abdullah Al Mamun said: “With features like AI Image to Video 2.0, the Honor 600S 5G gives users new ways to express their creativity. We want to make AI more accessible through practical tools that allow users to experiment, create and personalize their smartphone experiences.”
The device is powered by an 8100mAh battery with 45W fast charging support, delivering over 21 hours of continuous video social app usage or more than 15 hours of heavy gaming in daily usage scenarios.
For everyday performance, the smartphone features the Snapdragon® 4 Gen 4 processor, supported by 8GB of physical RAM and an additional 16GB of RAM expansion.
The device comes with IP68, IP69 and IP69K ratings, along with an SGS-certified 2.5-metre drop-resistance claim.
Available in Velvet Black, Desert Gold and Misty Purple, Honor 600S 5G is priced at Tk45,999.

Titumir: 73% of insurance claims remain unpaid amid irregularities over past 15yrs
item.description:
Around 73% of insurance claims in Bangladesh remain unpaid, with Tk7,779 crore outstanding out of total claims worth Tk10,611 crore, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir said on Wednesday.
He blamed political influence, irregularities and mismanagement over the past 15 years for the financial losses suffered by ordinary people, urging investigative journalists to expose corruption and the lack of accountability in the sector.
Titumir made the remarks as the chief guest at a programme marking the renewal of a group insurance agreement for members of the Dhaka Reporters Unity (DRU) at its Segunbagicha auditorium.
He said the insurance sector’s problems had received less attention than banking-sector scams, despite serious shortcomings in protecting policyholders and settling claims.
Of the country’s 72 life and non-life insurance companies, 60 received licences during different tenures of the Awami League government, he said. The non-life insurance sector is in an even worse position, with a claim settlement rate of just 11.3%.
The adviser urged journalists to go beyond reporting unpaid claims and investigate why settlements remain outstanding, identify those responsible and highlight the impact on policyholders.
He also called for greater transparency and accountability across banks, insurance companies and non-bank financial institutions, warning that the public would ultimately bear the burden of financial mismanagement and rising foreign debt.
At the programme, the DRU renewed its group insurance agreement with National Life Insurance Company for another year, covering around 2,000 members aged between 20 and 60.
Under the scheme, members’ families will receive Tk3 lakh in case of natural death and Tk3.8 lakh for accidental death. Coverage also includes Tk1 lakh for loss of limbs and Tk70,000 for surgery related to critical illness.
The event also saw the handover of a Tk3 lakh death claim to the family of DRU member Abu Hena Rasel and Tk70,000 in critical illness benefits to member Rafiqul Islam.

UGC scraps decision to suspend university admission tests
item.description:
The University Grants Commission (UGC) has scrapped its November 9 decision on admission procedures at public universities for the 2026-27 academic year, allowing institutions to conduct their own admission processes.
At a special meeting on Wednesday evening, chaired by UGC Chairman Professor Mamun Ahmed, the commission unanimously decided that universities could determine their admission procedures in line with their respective laws, statutes, regulations, policies and decisions of the relevant academic authorities.
The meeting was attended by all UGC members and public university vice-chancellors, who joined virtually.
The November 9 meeting had requested public universities to postpone admission tests until the publication of results for students seeking re-evaluation of their 2026 HSC results and those taking supplementary examinations.
However, the decision led to confusion over the universities’ academic autonomy, prompting the commission to convene Wednesday’s meeting to clarify the matter.
After reviewing the universities’ legal authority and institutional autonomy, the meeting unanimously agreed to cancel the earlier decision and reaffirmed their right to independently determine admission procedures within the applicable legal framework.
The UGC also stressed that universities’ autonomy in academic matters and the interests of students should be taken into account when conducting admissions.

Khulna bus services via Padma Bridge suspended over safety concerns
item.description:
Bus services from Khulna on all routes via the Padma Bridge have been suspended over security concerns, leaving passengers travelling to Dhaka, Chittagong, Cox’s Bazar and other destinations facing difficulties.
Services to Barisal via Gopalganj have also been halted. Many passengers arriving at Khulna’s bus terminal and ticket counters found no buses available.
The suspension followed incidents on Wednesday afternoon in which tree trunks were placed across roads at several points between Gopalganj and Kashiani, obstructing traffic. Several buses were also vandalised and pelted with bricks and stones.
The blockades were reportedly staged by activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its student wing, Bangladesh Chhatra League. Bus operators said they decided to suspend services to ensure the safety of passengers and vehicles.
Khulna Motor Workers’ Union President Md Zahid Hossain Khan told Dhaka Tribune that buses had been attacked and pelted with stones at several locations in Gopalganj on Wednesday noon.
“Amid concerns over the safety of passengers and vehicles, transport owners decided to suspend bus services after 1:30pm,” he said.
He said the suspension covered long-distance buses on the Khulna-Dhaka route via Gopalganj and the Padma Bridge, as well as services to Dhaka, Cox’s Bazar, Sylhet, Chittagong, Barisal and Rajbari.
Buses travelling from Khulna and Jessore via Narail and Kashiani to the Padma Bridge have also been suspended.
“Only buses using the previous route via Aricha are operating. We have no other option. We had to take this decision due to a lack of security,” he added.

item.title: Police foils garment workers’ road blockade attempt in Mirpur
item.description:
Garment workers demanding a minimum wage attempted to block roads in Mirpur on Wednesday evening, prompting police to fire sound grenades and tear gas to disperse them.
The incident took place in the Mirpur-11 area, where police moved in to clear the road.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Mirpur Division Deputy Commissioner Hasan Nasher Rikabdar said workers tried to block the road in the evening, but police dispersed them.
Earlier in the day, workers clashed with police twice in Kafrul and Pallabi.
Around noon, a chase and counter-chase broke out near the Mirpur-12 bus stand intersection, continuing for about half an hour. Police eventually removed the workers from the main road.
In the morning, clashes and brick-throwing were reported in Kafrul following allegations that several female workers had been harassed. Police fired around 10 sound grenades to bring the situation under control.
The incident occurred near Load Star Fashion and Mid Asia Fashion factories in Mirpur-14.
Police said the two factories employ around 5,100 workers. Workers from the factories allegedly disrupted production at nearby Jockey Garments, Vision Garments and Ideas Garments before bringing workers out of those facilities.
The workers accused several local BNP leaders and activists of harassing female workers. The allegations triggered clashes, including chases and brick-throwing, before police dispersed the workers and restored order.

item.title: Fire guts Sattola slum, leaving over 100 families with nothing
item.description:
A devastating fire tore through Sattola slum in the capital around 9am on Wednesday, destroying the homes and belongings of more than 100 families and leaving them without shelter or a means of earning a living.
No casualties were reported. But for the residents, who have seen such disasters before, the loss was near total.
Eight units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence brought the blaze under control at 11:15am after around one and a half hours of firefighting.
Nazma Akter heard screams and cries of alarm around 9am. Initially, she thought the flames would not reach her home and did not attempt to move any belongings.
But moments later, when she went downstairs, she saw the fire spreading towards their house.
She managed to escape with her husband and son, but could not take anything with her. Within minutes, the family’s home and everything they owned were reduced to ashes.
She moved to the area from Keraniganj four years ago. For the past two years, the family had been renting two rooms for Tk3,000 a month. Her father-in-law lived in one room, while Nazma, her husband and their son occupied the other.
With her husband working irregularly as a day labourer, Nazma earned money through sewing to help support the family.
But the fire destroyed her two sewing machines, along with furniture, fans, clothes and other household belongings. While retrieving the burnt remains of her sewing machines, she broke down, saying: “Everything is finished for me.”
The machines were her family’s main source of income. Now, apart from the clothes they were wearing when they fled, almost nothing remains.
For Aleya Begum, who has lived in the same area for around 40 years, the latest fire brought back painful memories.
She earns a living working as a domestic helper and lives with her two grandchildren, who attend a local madrasa. Every morning, she leaves home in search of work and returns at the end of the day to their small home.
Aleya said that while trying to remove their belongings during Wednesday’s fire, several items were stolen from their home.
Although her house narrowly escaped the latest blaze, she said an earlier fire had destroyed all their household possessions.
According to Aleya, she has witnessed at least five fires in the slum over the past two to three years. Despite the repeated losses, she said, affected residents have received little assistance from the authorities.
She also expressed frustration with local representatives, saying they make promises and speak sweetly to residents during election campaigns but rarely come forward when people lose everything in a disaster.
At an on-site briefing after the fire was brought under control, Lieutenant Colonel Md Mahmudul Hasan, director (operations and maintenance) of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, said the first unit reached the scene at 10:10am, with additional units deployed as the fire intensified.
He said the blaze had damaged tin-shed and semi-pucca houses in the densely populated low-income settlement. More than 100 families lived in the affected area, according to an initial assessment.
The official told Dhaka Tribune at 5:45pm that the cause of the fire and the extent of the damage had yet to be determined.
“We are working on it. I have personally visited the area and seen that more than 100 families have lost everything,” he said.
He added that an investigation committee would be formed to determine the cause of the fire and assess the losses after firefighting and damping operations were completed.
Fires are not new to Sattola slum. Major incidents were reported there in 2012, 2015, 2016, 2020, 2021 and 2025, destroying numerous homes. Several smaller fires had also broken out in different parts of the slum over the years.
Electrical short circuits have frequently been cited as a possible cause of such incidents. Weak and substandard electrical wiring, often installed through unauthorised connections, increases fire risks in the settlement.
The closely packed houses, built largely with bamboo, wood, tin and plastic, allow flames to spread rapidly. Gas cylinder use, leaking unauthorised gas connections and narrow access roads also make fire incidents particularly dangerous and difficult for emergency responders to tackle.
Following the fire, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton visited the affected area on Wednesday afternoon and announced immediate food, medical and rehabilitation support for the victims.
Speaking to reporters, he said the cause of the fire had yet to be established and that an investigation was underway to determine whether it was triggered by an electrical short circuit or another reason.
He said the visit followed direct instructions from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who represents the Dhaka-17 constituency.
According to the DNCC, a medical camp was set up for injured residents, while meals were arranged for affected families for Wednesday and Thursday. The city corporation is also preparing a list of affected families to provide financial assistance.
The administration said immediate financial assistance was distributed among affected families on behalf of the prime minister at 3pm on Wednesday.
Shafiqul Islam Khan further said the government would rebuild the damaged homes to their previous condition as soon as the debris was cleared.
He also said landowners had been instructed not to collect rent from affected families for the next two months or issue eviction notices requiring them to leave within the next year.
A special monitoring cell and committee would also be formed to oversee the rehabilitation and relief operations and prevent irregularities, according to the DNCC.
DNCC Slum Development Officer Md Humayun Kabir Khan told Dhaka Tribune that residents whose birth certificates had been destroyed in the fire could apply to the city corporation through the prescribed process to obtain replacement copies.
Each semi-pucca house in the slum accommodated at least two to three families. Some rented a single room, while others occupied two rooms, paying between Tk1,500 and Tk4,000 in monthly rent.
The slum falls within Dhaka-17, the parliamentary constituency represented by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, and is located close to a DNCC regional office.
