item.title: Legal notice urges govt to bring back Hasina within 15 days
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government, demanding that former prime minister Sheikh Hasina be brought back from India through diplomatic channels to face legal proceedings in Bangladesh.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun sent the notice on Wednesday, describing his move as a non-partisan effort to protect national sovereignty, territorial integrity and public security under Article 21(1) of the constitution.
The notice was sent by registered post and email to the Cabinet secretary, foreign secretary, public security division secretary, law secretary, inspector general of police and Bangladesh's high commissioner in New Delhi.
It raises concerns over the possibility of sensitive state information, including details of the country's defence system, intelligence network, diplomatic protocols and national security, being exposed during Hasina's prolonged stay in a neighbouring country.
The notice also cites the cases of former Yemeni president Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi and former Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych to highlight potential geopolitical risks associated with former leaders taking refuge abroad.
The lawyer has proposed a series of diplomatic and administrative measures, including sending a formal diplomatic note to India seeking cooperation in Hasina's safe return.
He also suggested arranging for her to enter the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi and surrender to Bangladeshi authorities, followed by her formal arrest by a special police team.
The notice further proposes issuing her a travel pass or permit and bringing her back to Dhaka under police escort by commercial or chartered flight.
It also suggests declaring Hasina's ancestral home in Tungipara, Gopalganj, a special sub-jail and transferring her there by helicopter after her arrival in Dhaka.
The notice says Hasina should be allowed to exercise her right to appeal against her conviction under Section 21 of the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973. It also proposes virtual court proceedings in her other pending civil and criminal cases to address security concerns.

item.title: UN expert: ICJ verdict on Myanmar could be ‘step towards justice’ for Rohingya
item.description:
As the International Court of Justice (ICJ) prepares to deliver its judgment in the genocide case against Myanmar, a UN human rights expert has said the decision could mark an important step towards justice for the Rohingya. She also warned that continuing violence and insecurity make their safe return from Bangladesh impossible at present.
Kelley E Currie, UN Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in Myanmar, said the judgment in the case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar would be an important moment for the Rohingya, Myanmar and the international community.
“This decision represents a potential step away from that impunity, and a potential step towards accountability for the perpetrators and justice for the survivors and the victims,” she said at her end-of-mission press conference at the UN house in Dhaka on Wednesday.
“We hope this verdict will recognise these crimes, call them by their right name and put us on the path towards justice.”
The ICJ, the United Nations’ principal judicial organ, is scheduled to deliver its judgment at 10am on Thursday in The Hague.
The case concerns Myanmar’s alleged violations of the 1948 Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, commonly known as the Genocide Convention.
For the more than 1.2 million Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, the judgment comes amid continuing uncertainty over whether conditions will ever allow them to return safely to their homes in Myanmar.
Currie said crimes committed against the Rohingya, including dispossession, denial of identity, forced displacement, torture, sexual violence and murder, “did not begin or end in 2017”. Too many perpetrators had escaped accountability, she said, and too many victims had been denied justice.
If the judgment recognised the crimes, all nations would have a duty to support its full implementation, she said.
“Regardless of the outcome, these survivors, their community and their supporters around the world will never stop demanding justice and fighting for an end to impunity. I stand with them,” she said.
Currie called on countries maintaining business and other forms of engagement with Myanmar’s military authorities to reconsider their involvement.
She argued that continued economic and other support could enable the authorities to sustain violence and displacement. She urged governments to use pressure, including sanctions and measures to restrict sources of support, to discourage such engagement.
She also called on regional and international actors to stop actions that contribute to violence against civilians and to press Myanmar’s authorities to end abuses.
In her written statement, Currie said the authorities in Naypyidaw bore primary responsibility for the current crisis.
“The path to peace in Myanmar does not run through Naypyidaw,” she said.
Currie urged Bangladesh and international partners to adopt a comprehensive approach to the Rohingya crisis. She warned that worsening insecurity in refugee camps, declining humanitarian assistance and continued conflict in Myanmar were undermining prospects for safe and dignified returns.
Bangladesh continues to host more than one million Rohingya and other refugees from Myanmar who cannot return home safely because of the ongoing human rights and humanitarian crisis, she said.
Deadly attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure continue amid intense fighting, particularly in Rakhine State.
Rohingya and other marginalised communities also face repression and severe deprivation of their civil, political, economic and cultural rights in areas controlled by both the authorities in Naypyidaw and the Arakan Army.
“These conditions not only make safe, dignified, and durable returns impossible for Rohingya refugees but are making life inside Myanmar increasingly dangerous,” she said.
The situation has also made humanitarian assistance inside Rakhine State more difficult, while donor support continues to decline.
Currie said the budget for refugee assistance in Bangladesh had reached an all-time low even as the population requiring assistance was at an all-time high.
Currie noted that Bangladesh’s newly elected government had formed a special committee to develop a comprehensive strategy for the early, safe, voluntary and dignified return of Rohingya refugees and others to Myanmar.
The final strategy has not yet been released. Currie said its proposed priorities included:
During her November 11–18 visit, she met senior government officials in Dhaka and travelled to Cox’s Bazar, where she met refugees, community members and organisations working in the camps.
Currie said insecurity was a common concern among the refugees she met, particularly for women and children.
She recounted hearing from women and girls afraid to leave their homes, mothers worried that their children could be abducted, and men who felt powerless when they and their families were abused by thugs and criminals.
She also raised concerns about precarious shelter for people who had arrived since 2024 and the vulnerabilities faced by religious minorities within the Rohingya community.
Insecurity and lawlessness, combined with a lack of meaningful economic and educational opportunities, were driving harmful coping strategies among refugees and host communities. These included drug use and trafficking, smuggling, human trafficking, recruitment into criminal or armed groups, and online gambling, she said.
Currie called for urgent improvements in camp security, including the removal, disarmament and disincentivisation of unauthorised armed actors, whether armed groups or criminal organisations.
She warned that recent donor cuts, particularly to protection, education, livelihoods and non-emergency healthcare, had worsened the situation.
“Further reductions in support risk creating a generation of young people with no hope and nothing to lose,” she said.
Currie cautioned that localisation of humanitarian assistance must not become an excuse for further funding cuts. Instead, it should involve strengthening local institutions, investing in the capacities of refugee and host communities, improving social cohesion and reforming camp management to ensure greater refugee representation and participation.
Currie described Myanmar’s conflict as part of a decades-long struggle over the country’s future. She contrasted an exclusionary state dominated by a military elite with the prospect of a federal democracy that respects the rights and dignity of all communities.
Inclusive political dialogue involving the Rohingya and other marginalised groups was essential to resolving the crisis, she said. She urged regional countries and other UN member states to support meaningful engagement among key stakeholders and to refrain from actions that contribute to violence against civilians.
She also called for a shift away from a charity-based approach that treats refugees merely as beneficiaries, towards a rights-based approach recognising them as people entitled to participate in decisions about their future.
Currie, who has been denied entry to Myanmar, said she would develop more detailed recommendations for relevant stakeholders. She will present a full report on her Bangladesh visit at the March 2027 session of the UN Human Rights Council.

item.title: Ex-state minister Hiru, two others sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday sent former state minister for water resources Lt Col (retd) Mohammad Nazrul Islam Hiru and two others to jail in an Anti-Terrorism Act case filed with Banani Police Station.
The other accused are Kazi Mostafizul Islam Mukta and Barrister Rana Tajuddin Khan.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order following a petition by the investigation officer, Inspector Mohammad Abul Matin of the Detective Branch of police.
During the hearing, state lawyer Shamsuddoha Sumon argued in favour of showing the accused arrested and sought their detention. Defence lawyer Khaleda Jahan Lily opposed the move and sought bail.
She told the court that one of the accused, a Bir Protik award recipient, was elderly and had returned home from Combined Military Hospital (CMH) two days earlier after receiving treatment. However, the court did not hear the bail petition as the case documents were unavailable.
According to the case statement, a group of 100 to 120 people staged a torch procession on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway opposite the Army Stadium in Banani around 12:20am on August 7.
The processionists allegedly chanted slogans demanding the withdrawal of the ban on the activities of the Awami League and its associate organisation, Chhatra League, and the release of political prisoners.
Police arrested seven people in connection with the incident and seized 70 partially burnt torches, a banner and 70 black masks from the scene, the complaint said.
The investigation officer told the court that information obtained from the three accused was being scrutinised. Further interrogation might be necessary to identify and arrest other suspects and establish the circumstances of the incident.
The officer also expressed concern that the accused could hamper the investigation or go into hiding if released on bail, seeking their detention until the investigation is completed.

item.title: Arson attack on BNP office in Netrokona, nearby shop gutted
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to the BNP office of Chiram union in Barhatta upazila of Netrokona early Wednesday, destroying the office and an adjacent firewood shop.
The fire broke out at around 4am at Bamangaon Bazar in Chiram union, according to police and local sources.
A group of miscreants allegedly set fire to the union BNP office, and the flames quickly spread to the neighbouring firewood shop.
On information, firefighters rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control. By then, both the office and the shop had been gutted.
Barhatta police station Officer-in-Charge Champak Dam told Dhaka Tribune that the initial suspicion was that miscreants had deliberately set fire to the office.
He said the adjacent shop was also damaged in the fire, adding that those involved had yet to be identified.
The police officer said the incident was being investigated and legal action would be taken accordingly.

item.title: Lawyer beaten at court premises sent to jail
item.description:
A pro-Awami League lawyer and Jubo League leader who was beaten by an agitated crowd on the court premises has been sent to jail along with two others in a case over a crude bomb explosion outside the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court in Dhaka.
The three accused — Advocate Dr Shamim Al Saiful Sohag, Obaidur Rahman Sudaich and Md Sumaiyaz Islam — were sent to jail on Wednesday after Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Zakir Hossain rejected their bail petitions.
State lawyer Mohammad Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the order.
Police had produced the accused before the court and sought their detention in custody until the investigation was completed. The investigation officer, Sub-Inspector Anupam Das of Sutrapur Police Station, said they had admitted their involvement during preliminary interrogation.
Defence lawyers sought bail, while the prosecution opposed the petitions. Sohag, who is also a lawyer, told the court that he had been dragged out of a courtroom and assaulted by a crowd on Tuesday while attending a hearing in former Dhaka South City Corporation mayor Sayeed Khokon's remand case. He said he had been held for nearly an hour and lost consciousness during the assault.
“I came to court as a lawyer, but they turned me into an accused,” he told the court, denying any involvement in the November 9 explosion.
The prosecution argued that the accused were involved in the attack and opposed their release. The magistrate said police had found preliminary evidence linking them to the incident and noted that the case had been filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act, making bail inappropriate at this stage.
According to the case statement, crude bombs exploded near the main entrance of the CMM Court on the evening of November 9, creating panic. Around 25 to 30 unidentified people were allegedly involved, and two suspects were detained with the help of police and people present at the scene.
A case was filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act and Explosives Act by a Sutrapur police sub-inspector the following day.
Police later identified Sohag, Sudaich and Sumaiyaz as suspects based on the investigation. On Tuesday night, police took them into custody from an agitated crowd in front of Government Kabi Nazrul College in Sutrapur.
Sohag was injured in the crowd's assault and received treatment at Sir Salimullah Medical College Hospital.

item.title: Traffic police box set ablaze in Chittagong
item.description:
Miscreants set fire to a traffic police box in Muradpur, Chittagong, early Wednesday, prompting police to launch an investigation to identify those involved.
The incident took place around 1am. The fire failed to spread inside the box as its windows were closed, causing no major damage. No one was injured.
Police and local sources said several people set the box on fire before fleeing. Local residents later spotted the flames and brought the fire under control.
No police personnel were inside the box at the time. Officers learned about the incident in the morning.
Panchlaish Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mozammel Haque said police had collected CCTV footage and were examining it to identify those responsible.
He said the suspects had not yet been identified and legal action would be taken once they were traced.

item.title: Nearly 300 arrested as garment unrest flares in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
Garment workers staged protests and clashed with police in several areas of Savar and Ashulia on Wednesday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Police fired tear gas, sound grenades and rubber bullets to disperse demonstrators, leaving several people, including police personnel, injured.
Nearly 300 people have been arrested in 24 cases filed with Savar and Ashulia police stations over alleged acts of sabotage linked to the unrest, police said.
Most factories resumed production in the morning, but workers at several factories stopped work, while some attempted to block roads. At least 20 factories in Ashulia were closed on Wednesday, according to industrial police.
In Savar's Ulail area, workers from Al-Muslim and several other factories blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway around 2:30pm, bringing traffic to a standstill. Clashes broke out when industrial police reached the scene and workers allegedly threw bricks at them. Police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets. The workers withdrew from the highway around 4pm.
In Ashulia, workers attempted to block the Abdullahpur-Baipail road in Narsinghapur around 10:15am. Police chased them away and fired tear gas. Workers from nearby factories also allegedly attacked MK Apparels in Khejurbagan, damaging its gate, reception-area glass and a vehicle's windscreen.
Industrial police said 20 factories were closed, including some shut indefinitely under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act. Other factories declared general holidays, while production continued normally in many establishments.
Police also arrested two leaders of the Green Bangla Garments Workers Federation — its president Mosammat Sultana Begum and general secretary Md Ilias — from Pallabi in Dhaka on Tuesday night over allegations of inciting unrest and threatening factory owners and labour leaders. Local residents in Hemayetpur detained another labour leader, Humayun Kabir, and handed him over to police on Wednesday.
Police said the 24 cases filed in connection with the unrest had led to nearly 300 arrests.
Meanwhile, law enforcement agencies increased patrols and surveillance across the industrial belt to prevent further violence. The unrest came ahead of a nationwide shutdown program called by the activities-banned Awami League for Thursday.

item.title: 71 Awami League activists detained in Dhaka in 24 hours
item.description:
At least 71 activists and leaders of the activities-banned Awami League and its various affiliated organizations have been detained by police in Dhaka over the past 24 hours. Police said more than 2kg of gunpowder was recovered from a group of them.
The information was announced in a message sent by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Media Division.
According to police, the gunpowder had been collected from a border area and brought to Dhaka for sabotage through a post-holding leader of Meherpur Chhatra League.
Police said a small amount of the gunpowder was later ignited at a house in the Mirpur area to test its effectiveness.
After receiving information, detectives detained 3 activists and leaders of the Awami League and Chhatra League from the house, along with the gunpowder.

item.title: Tungipara violence: Police station, security vehicles, MP’s home torched overnight
item.description:
Tungipara in Gopalganj witnessed widespread violence overnight as protesters attacked a police station, set fire to security vehicles and torched at least 20 houses, including the residence of local lawmaker SM Zilani.
The violence was reportedly triggered by the arrest of several people on Tuesday night on suspicion of sabotage ahead of the activities-banned Awami League’s November 19 lockdown program.
According to local residents and eyewitnesses, loudspeaker announcements were made demanding the release of those arrested. Later, groups of protesters, including leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations, attacked Tungipara Police Station, vandalising and setting fire to the building.
The situation escalated when law enforcement agencies moved to bring the violence under control. Several people were injured in the ensuing clashes, including two reportedly hit by bullets, according to local sources.
Meanwhile, a BGB team reached Nilfa Bazar in Tungipara after reports of a road blockade. Clashes broke out between BGB members and protesters in several rounds.
Law enforcement personnel fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the crowds.
At one point, protesters allegedly set fire to several police vehicles, at least four police and BGB vehicles, and an armoured vehicle, local sources said.
At least 20 houses in the area were also reportedly set ablaze, including the residence of Gopalganj-3 MP SM Zilani.
A visit to different parts of Tungipara on Wednesday morning revealed signs of widespread destruction. No law enforcement personnel were seen in several areas, while tree trunks and electricity poles had been placed across roads to block traffic.
The blockades disrupted movement in different parts of the upazila.
In contrast, the situation in Gopalganj town remained largely normal despite a relatively limited presence of law enforcement personnel. Shops were open and traffic was moving normally.

item.title: RMG workers block Dhaka-Aricha highway over minimum wage demand
item.description:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway in Savar, demanding an increase in the minimum wage, prompting law enforcement agencies to fire tear gas to disperse them.
The protest began around 2:30pm on Wednesday when workers from several garment factories gathered on the highway, halting traffic and triggering severe congestion.
As of 3:20pm, the protesters were still occupying the highway and chanting slogans demanding fulfilment of their demands.
Savar Highway Police Station In-Charge Ali Ahmed said workers had taken to the highway over their minimum wage demand.
He said authorities were trying to bring the situation under control, persuade the workers to leave the road and restore normal traffic.

item.title: BNP parliamentary party meeting begins amid reports of violence
item.description:
The BNP parliamentary party on Wednesday afternoon held a meeting at the National Parliament Building amid reports of violence allegedly involving Awami League activists in different parts of the country.
The meeting began at around 2:30pm, with Prime Minister and Leader of the House Tarique Rahman in the chair, on the final day of the current session of parliament, said Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
BNP parliamentary party members attended the meeting.
Talking to UNB, several BNP MPs said the recent violence in Gopalganj and some other parts of the country would come up for discussion, along with the party's next course of action.
Party sources said the meeting would also discuss the party's parliamentary activities and other issues.

item.title: ADB deepens support to mobilize private investment in Bangladesh
item.description:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has reaffirmed its commitment to helping Bangladesh attract long-term private investment, diversify its economy, and expand sustainable infrastructure financing.
During November 16-18, ADB Director General (DG) for South Asia Sona Shrestha led a One-ADB delegation to Dhaka for high-level discussions with government, regulatory, private sector, and development partners.
The delegation included Takeo Koike, head of ADB’s Office of Markets Development and Public–Private Partnership, and Craig Lee Roberts, senior adviser in ADB’s Private Sector Operations Department.
“Bangladesh’s next phase of growth will require deeper financial markets, a stronger investment climate, and reforms that enable private enterprise to invest, innovate, and create jobs,” said DG Shrestha.
“ADB will continue to bring together its public and private sector expertise to help translate the country’s development priorities into bankable investments.”
The delegation discussed banking, taxation, and state-owned enterprise reforms; development of bond and equity markets; and wider access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises with Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman, Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Masud Khan, Invest Bangladesh Chairman Ashik Chowdhury, and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tanvir Shahriar Ghani.
During the visit, the Finance and Planning Minister joined ADB in launching PPP Monitor: Bangladesh, which uses more than 500 indicators to identify barriers to private investment in infrastructure.
ADB also signed an agreement to extend its transaction advisory support to five additional solar and battery storage projects.
The expanded pipeline now covers six projects with more than 1,000 megawatts of planned capacity and is expected to help mobilize over $1 billion in private investment.
Discussions with businesses and development partners will also inform the master plan for Bangladesh’s Integrated Growth Network Development initiative and ADB’s country partnership strategy for 2028–2032.

item.title: Top Glove offers Bangladeshi workers opportunity via zero-cost ethical recruitment
item.description:
Malaysia-based multinational company Top Glove Sdn. Bhd. is offering Bangladeshi workers an opportunity to secure overseas employment through a 100% zero-cost recruitment model, aimed at ensuring transparent, ethical and financially secure recruitment.
As one of the world's leading glove manufacturers, Top Glove provides employment opportunities, structured working environments and prospects for long-term employment to workers from different countries.
The key feature of this initiative is that workers are not required to pay recruitment fees to secure employment.
Recruitment-related expenses are to be borne by the employer, helping protect workers from excessive charges, intermediaries and financial exploitation.
The approach is consistent with the responsible recruitment principles promoted by the International Labour Organization (ILO).
Overseas employment is an important source of income for many Bangladeshi families.
However, high recruitment costs have traditionally placed considerable financial pressure on workers and their families.
Top Glove's employer-funded recruitment model offers an opportunity to demonstrate that international employment can be arranged without transferring recruitment costs to workers.
The initiative could also establish a positive precedent for Bangladesh–Malaysia manpower cooperation.
The recruitment initiative has attracted negative reactions and criticism on social media and in certain media outlets.
While transparency, accountability and workers' welfare deserve scrutiny, criticism should remain factual, fair and proportionate.
Concerns regarding selection procedures, recruitment transparency and workers' rights should be addressed openly.
However, judging the entire initiative solely on the basis of operational difficulties during interview arrangements may overlook its broader employment objectives.
Unfair or misleading publicity could also discourage international employers from considering Bangladesh for future recruitment opportunities.
The interview arrangements encountered some difficulties. Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited (BOESL) was responsible for the interview venue, coordination and security arrangements.
However, the process did not proceed as smoothly as expected, creating operational challenges and affecting the overall interview experience.
Such shortcomings should encourage all stakeholders to review the process, improve institutional coordination and ensure professional arrangements for future recruitment exercises rather than focusing solely on assigning blame.
The success of zero-cost recruitment requires coordinated efforts from the employer, Bangladesh Government, BOESL and relevant recruitment and training partners. Clear responsibilities, effective communication, proper documentation and transparent selection procedures are essential.
Most importantly, no agent, sub-agent, intermediary or unauthorized individual should demand payment from candidates under this program.
Top Glove's initiative offers an opportunity to strengthen Bangladesh–Malaysia employment cooperation while promoting ethical recruitment and migrant worker protection.
For Bangladeshi workers, it represents the prospect of employment with an established international company without the burden of recruitment costs.
For Top Glove, Bangladesh remains a potential source of capable and hardworking employees.
Rather than allowing operational challenges or negative publicity to overshadow the initiative, stakeholders should work together to strengthen the recruitment process, protect workers' interests and encourage responsible international employers.

item.title: HSBC highlights cybersecurity, digital resilience for organizational preparedness
item.description:
The Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Bangladesh recently organized Cyber Security and Digital Resilience events for its corporate customers in Dhaka and Chattogram.
The events brought together Chief Financial Officers (CFOs), Chief Technology Officers (CTOs) and other senior representatives from different corporate clients and key stakeholders to discuss the evolving cyber threat landscape and the importance of strengthening organizational preparedness.
The sessions highlighted the growing complexity of cyber threats and the need for businesses to develop robust capabilities to identify, prevent and respond to potential risks.
Discussions also focus on the increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI), which, while creating new opportunities for business and innovation, is also enabling cybercriminals to launch more sophisticated, targeted and scalable attacks.
The rise of AI-generated impersonations, deepfakes and increasingly convincing phishing attempts makes digital vigilance and resilience more important than ever.
Todd Stewart, chief information security officer, International Markets, HSBC, delivered the keynote address, highlighting the importance of digital transformation and data protection.
He said: “It was so remarkable to see the level of genuine interest and engagement from the audience, which really showed how Cyber Security is at the front of everyone’s mind. HSBC is continuing to prioritize investment in Cyber Security ensuring that we can stay ahead of the emerging threats and protect our customers well into the future.”
He also highlighted HSBC’s continued investment in digital innovation and its efforts to strengthen protection for clients against associated cyber risks and continues to enhance its cybersecurity capabilities through multiple layers of security controls, round-the-clock security monitoring, cyber intelligence and threat analysis, and continuous improvements in its ability to prevent, detect, respond to and recover from cyber threats.
HSBC continues to leverage its extensive global network, advanced digital platforms and deep market expertise to help businesses navigate complexity, strengthen resilience and unlock new opportunities for sustainable growth.

item.title: Youth hacked to death for filming gang attack in Narayanganj
item.description:
A 25-year-old man was hacked to death in Fatullah of Narayanganj for recording a gang attack on his mobile phone on Tuesday night.
The victim, Yusuf Molla, was attacked around 8pm in the Shiachar Takkar Math area. He died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital around 12:30 am. Yusuf, son of Mofiz Molla from Berki village in Chandpur, worked as a driver and lived in a rented house in the area.
According to locals, a group of 40-50 armed men attacked the house of Delwar Hossain Delu, a BNP member from Ward 9 of Kutubpur union, vandalising the property. The attackers were carrying machetes, knives and other locally made weapons.
Yusuf, who lived in a neighbouring house, was filming the attack when the assailants noticed him and tried to seize his phone. As he resisted, they hacked him indiscriminately before fleeing. His family first took him to Khanpur 300-bed Hospital before transferring him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital as his condition deteriorated.
Delu alleged that the attack stemmed from an earlier dispute involving local Krishak Dal leader Jewel Arman, who had allegedly extorted Tk8 lakh from him in June. A case over the incident is pending in court.
Narayanganj Additional Superintendent of Police Mohammad Shamim Hossain said the attack followed a clash between the two groups earlier in the day. He confirmed that Yusuf was attacked for filming the incident and said legal action would be taken against those involved.

item.title: Cyclone Akvan leaves fishermen stranded as Bay turns rough
item.description:
Barely days after the previous storm disrupted fishing activities, another cyclone, Akvan, has formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining west-central Bay, prompting authorities to hoist distant warning Signal No 2 at all four seaports.
The rough sea has left fishermen in distress, particularly those who ventured into the deep sea for fishing. Many have been forced to take shelter on different islands and shoals around Dublar Char near the Sundarbans estuary. The disruption has also brought dry fish production to a near standstill, leaving workers at the island's fishing settlements struggling to make ends meet.
With another cyclone forming just 12 days after the previous one, the Bay has turned rough once again. Unable to withstand the turbulent conditions in deep waters, fishermen have returned to nearby islands and coastal areas, disrupting fishing activities and threatening their seasonal earnings.
Several low-pressure systems and depressions, along with three cyclones, have formed over the Bay of Bengal this year. Cyclone Arnab developed over the central Bay on October 24 and made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28. Fishermen had just begun arriving in Dublar Char for the dry fish season when the storm disrupted their activities.
Another cyclone, Murashu, hit the southern Andhra Pradesh coast on November 3, further delaying fishing. A low-pressure system formed on November 13 and intensified into a depression on November 15 before developing into Cyclone Akvan on November 17-18. The storm is moving towards India's Andhra Pradesh coast.
Several other low-pressure systems and depressions also formed over the Bay in January, July, August and September.
Md Khalilur Rahman, acting officer-in-charge of the Dublar Char Forest Office, said fishermen had faced repeated setbacks since the beginning of the dry fish season.
Their journey to Dublar Char was delayed by Cyclone Arnab on October 30, followed by another disruption caused by Cyclone Murashu on November 3. Before even 15 days of the season had passed, Cyclone Akvan struck again, he said.
"Fishermen cannot venture into the sea because of the rough weather. They are also unable to dry fish on the platforms. As a result, they are spending idle days and suffering financial losses," he said.
Many fishermen are now struggling with debts and uncertainty, while the decline in dry fish production could also affect the Forest Department's revenue, he added.
According to a special weather bulletin issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department on Wednesday morning, Cyclone Akvan had intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining west-central Bay.
At 6am on November 18, its centre was located 1,280km southwest of Chittagong, 1,220km southwest of Cox's Bazar, 1,185km southwest of Mongla and 1,170km southwest of Payra seaports.
The storm was moving north-northwestwards and was likely to cross India's Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20 as a severe cyclonic storm.
The maximum sustained wind speed near its centre was 89kmph, with gusts reaching up to 117kmph. The sea remained very rough near the storm's centre.
The meteorological department advised fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay to remain close to the coast and navigate with caution until further notice.
Despite the warning, coastal areas of Khulna, Bagerhat and Satkhira experienced intermittent sunshine and cloudy conditions on Wednesday. Water levels in local rivers were slightly higher than normal, although river transport remained unaffected. The deep sea, however, remained rough.
Shankar Kumar Bihari, a fisherman taking shelter on Dublar Char, said they had faced repeated disruptions since arriving for the dry fish season.
"We were caught in Cyclone Arnab at the beginning of the season. Before even 15 days had passed, Akvan struck again. We have now left the sea and taken shelter on the island," he said.
He added that July had also been difficult for fishermen because of successive low-pressure systems. Although conditions improved briefly in early August, two consecutive low-pressure systems disrupted fishing again.
Whenever adverse weather makes the sea rough, fishermen are forced to return from deep waters, affecting their catches and income.
Earlier, three consecutive low-pressure systems formed over the Bay in July, one of which developed into a monsoon depression and another into a deep depression.
A low-pressure system also formed over the North Bay and adjoining West Bengal-Bangladesh coast on August 12. It subsequently intensified into a well-marked low-pressure system and then a land depression before weakening. Another low-pressure system formed on August 16, prolonging the difficulties for fishermen.

item.title: Rooppur plant delivers 350MW to national grid in 8.5hrs
item.description:
The first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant supplied 350 megawatts of electricity to the national grid during an eight-and-a-half-hour trial run on Tuesday, marking its first power injection into the grid.
The unit operated without any reported problems before being disconnected for further technical tests. It will be run again for several hours, although the date of the next trial has not yet been fixed.
Project Director Kabir Hossain told Dhaka Tribune that the plant had completed the initial run successfully. Power generation would be increased gradually, depending on the results of further tests.
The trial supply began at 3:16pm on Tuesday in the presence of Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam.
During the tests, engineers monitored the performance and stability of the turbine, generator and systems connecting the plant to the national grid.
Project officials said each stage would assess the plant’s systems, turbine and generator performance, and grid integration. If the results are satisfactory, the plant will require approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) before the next phase of trial operations.
Under an agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit is expected to undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning commercial power supply at full capacity.
Following the trial period, the unit will be provisionally handed over by the Russian contractor to the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission. The Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd (NPCBL) will subsequently begin operating the facility through a government gazette notification.

item.title: 45 young people showcase CHT stories through mobile video workshop
item.description:
Forty-five young people from the Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) have showcased stories about their communities through mobile videos produced during a three-day storytelling workshop in Rangamati.
Titled “Voices from the Hills”, the workshop concluded on Tuesday with a screening of participants’ videos highlighting local culture, livelihoods, challenges and resilience.
Organised by the Department of Journalism, Media and Communication at Daffodil International University (DIU), with support from UNDP Bangladesh’s ERRD-CHT Project, the workshop brought together participants from Rangamati, Khagrachhari and Bandarban.
The closing event was held at the Tourism Holiday Complex in Rangamati, where participants screened their completed videos and exchanged experiences with trainers and fellow participants.
On the final day, participants completed editing their footage, interviews and photographs under the guidance of trainers. They also received practical instruction on storytelling, shot selection, audio quality, captions and titles.
The workshop began on Sunday with sessions on storytelling techniques, human-centred story selection, storyboarding, mobile videography and video editing.
On Monday, participants visited communities in Rangamati to collect stories through interviews, photographs and video footage. Their work covered education, livelihoods, climate change, women's participation, youth aspirations, culture and environmental issues.
The training also emphasised informed consent, cultural sensitivity and respect for people's dignity when documenting and sharing community stories.
The sessions were facilitated by Dr Md Abdul Kabil Khan, associate professor and head of DIU's Department of Journalism, Media and Communication; Lecturer Meherun Nahar; and Lecturer Md Tanvir Rahman, with support from other department members.
Speaking at the closing session, Shareful Hassan, planning, monitoring and reporting analyst at UNDP Bangladesh's ERRD-CHT Project, said communities were experiencing changes in their everyday lives alongside technological and lifestyle transformations.
He stressed the importance of preserving local culture and heritage amid these changes.
Meher Nigar Bhuiyan, programme manager of the European Union's Resilient Livelihoods Programme, encouraged young people to use their creativity and skills to highlight everyday challenges, particularly the untold stories of marginalised communities in the CHT.
She expressed hope that the workshop would inspire further storytelling initiatives and help bring local experiences to a wider audience.
Supported by the European Union, the ERRD-CHT Project works across the three hill districts to promote inclusive education, climate resilience, biodiversity conservation, good governance, social cohesion and youth engagement.
The workshop aimed to strengthen young people's storytelling skills and amplify local voices through mobile video production.

AIUB Games 2026 opens with 3,200 participants
item.description:
The AIUB Games 2026 officially commenced with an inauguration ceremony at the American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB) campus on Tuesday, with approximately 3,200 participants from various academic departments.
The ceremony was inaugurated by Hasanul A Hasan, founder member and chairman of the Board of Trustees of AIUB, who attended the event and delivered remarks marking the formal commencement of the university-wide sporting event.
The ceremony was also attended by university officials, including Manzur H Khan, proctor of AIUB; Major (Retd) Faiz-Ul-Bari Rajon, deputy director of administration; and Md Joynal Abedin, coordinator of the Office of Sports, AIUB.
Students, faculty members and administrative officials also attended the ceremony.
The AIUB Games 2026 features 11 competitive segments, bringing together approximately 3,200 participants from different academic departments. The event provides participants with opportunities to demonstrate their athletic abilities, competitive spirit, teamwork and sportsmanship through various sporting disciplines.
Organized by the Office of Sports, AIUB, in collaboration with the Office of Student Affairs, the event reflects the university's commitment to promoting sports, physical well-being and holistic student development.
Beyond competition, the event also serves as a platform for strengthening interdepartmental engagement, fostering a sense of belonging and encouraging active participation in university life.

item.title: Tasnia Farin returns to OTT with dark comedy ‘Dakatiya Bashi’
Dhaka, Colombo agree to establish joint commission to strengthen ties
item.description:
Bangladesh and Sri Lanka on Wednesday signed a document to establish a Joint Consultative Commission for Comprehensive Cooperation to strengthen bilateral relations and institutionalise regular diplomatic engagement at the foreign ministerial level.
The memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed in Colombo following a bilateral meeting between State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir and Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath.
The memorandum of understanding (MoU) aims to create a formal mechanism for consultations on bilateral cooperation and issues of mutual interest.
The commission will facilitate bilateral meetings at the level of foreign ministers, providing a platform for reviewing existing cooperation and exploring opportunities to further strengthen relations between the two countries, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
During the meeting at Sri Lanka's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the two sides discussed recent political developments and economic challenges faced by their respective governments.
They also exchanged views on various initiatives undertaken by both countries to address those challenges.
The ministers expressed satisfaction over the exchange of high-level visits between Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, recognising their importance in strengthening mutual understanding and cooperation.
They underscored the value of continued high-level engagement to review bilateral relations and exchange views on regional and multilateral issues of common concern.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,329 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,329.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,224, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 105, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,376 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 252,173.
During the same period, 258 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 25,786.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 225,339 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 216,389 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Garment workers, BNP activists clash in Mirpur
item.description:
Garment workers clashed with local BNP activists in Kafrul, Mirpur, on Wednesday morning over allegations that several female workers had been harassed.
The incident took place around 9am near Load Star Fashion and Mid Asia Fashion factories in Mirpur-13, with both sides chasing each other and exchanging brickbats.
Police fired around 10 sound grenades to bring the situation under control.
Agitated workers also vandalized the windows of a Social Islami Bank branch in the Mymensingh Samity building and tore down a banner bearing the photograph of Dhaka North Administrator Md Shafiqul Islam Khan Milton.
According to police, the two factories employ around 5,000 workers. The unrest began after workers alleged that employees of nearby factories had disrupted their production activities and local BNP activists had harassed female workers.
Mirpur Division Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Zahidul Islam said the situation was now under control, with adequate police personnel deployed at the scene.

item.title: Ex-state minister Nazrul Islam Hiru arrested
item.description:
Former state minister for water resources Lt Col (retd) Mohammad Nazrul Islam Hiru has been arrested by the Special Response Battalion (SRB-01).
He was arrested during a raid at his residence in Baridhara DOHS in the capital around 7:30am on Wednesday.
A team led by SRB-01 ASP Lutfar conducted the operation.
Several arrest warrants had been issued against him in multiple cases, including those involving sabotage, according to the report.
Following his arrest, SRB personnel took him to the battalion headquarters in Uttara.
Hiru is a retired military officer, freedom fighter and Awami League politician.
He served as the MP for Narsingdi-1 for four consecutive terms from 2009 to 2024 and as state minister for water resources from 2014 to 2018.

item.title: 44 BGB platoons deployed in four districts amid workers' unrest
item.description:
A total of 44 platoons of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in industrial areas across Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj and Mymensingh to maintain law and order and assist the civil administration amid ongoing workers' unrest.
The BGB media wing shared the information on Wednesday.
Of the deployed personnel, 20 platoons are in Dhaka, covering Mirpur, Hemayetpur, Savar and Ashulia, including Yunus Convention Hall, Kathgara, Jirabo, Hamim Group, Midlar Group and Jamgara.
Another 15 platoons have been deployed in Gazipur, covering Chandra, Polli Bidyut, Mouchak, Konabari, Telirchala, Kashimpur, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha, Salna and Baishya Kuribari.
Seven platoons are stationed in Narayanganj, covering Shibu Market, Katherpul, Jalkuri, the BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara Mor, Kanchpur Bridge and Shimrail. The remaining two platoons are deployed in Bhaluka and Trishal in Mymensingh.
The BGB said its personnel were working in coordination with the local administration and police to maintain law and order in the industrial areas.
A monitoring cell at BGB headquarters is also reviewing live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other specialised equipment to monitor developments, facilitate the exchange of information and coordinate responses, the force said.

item.title: Fire at Sattola slum brought under control
item.description:
A fire at Sattola slum in the capital’s Mohakhali area was brought under control at 11am on Wednesday after eight Fire Service units responded to the blaze.
The fire broke out at around 9:40am, said Anwarul Islam, an official at the Fire Service media cell.
He said eight units were deployed to the scene, including three from Tejgaon Fire Station, two from Baridhara Fire Station and two from Kurmitola Fire Station.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage are yet to be determined.

item.title: Workers block Dhaka-Mymensingh highway again amid wage protests
item.description:
Garment workers have again blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in Gazipur, bringing traffic to a standstill amid ongoing protests demanding higher wages.
The blockade began around 9:45am on Wednesday, when workers from several garment factories in the Chhaydana area of Gazipur city took to the highway at Chhaydana and Hariken, halting traffic in both directions and causing severe disruption for commuters.
Industrial Police, local police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel reached the scene and are engaging with the workers to bring the situation under control.
Meanwhile, workers at SM Knit Wear in the Notun Bazar area of Sreepur, Golden Refit Garments in Bagher Bazar and Fakira Garments in Bhabanipur have stopped work and staged peaceful sit-ins on their factory floors.
In Konabari, workers from two other garment factories also staged protests but did not block the highway.
Amjad Hossain, superintendent of police for the Gazipur industrial zone, said efforts were underway to bring the situation under control.
He said 10 factories had declared a holiday on Wednesday amid the workers' unrest, while 39 factories had been closed indefinitely, based on reports received on Tuesday.
According to the Industrial Police, workers in the Gazipur industrial zone have been protesting for several days, demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
On Tuesday, workers staged demonstrations in several areas, including Konabari, Kashimpur, Chandna Chourasta, Jarun, Naojor, Chhaydana, Bhogra, and the C&B-2 and Apada areas of Sreepur.
The protests turned violent, with clashes involving brick-throwing, tear gas and sound grenades. Several people, including police officers, garment workers and journalists, were injured.
To prevent further unrest, authorities ordered the closure of 70 factories across the district from 11:30am on Tuesday.

item.title: Awami League office, ex-MP Bahar's home set on fire again in Comilla
item.description:
The Comilla South district office of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, and the residence and personal office of former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar were set on fire again on early Wednesday.
The incidents took place around 1am in the Ramghat and Munsef Bari areas of the city. This marks the third time Bahar's residence and political office have been attacked, vandalized and set on fire.
Videos circulating on social media show a group of BNP and its affiliated organisation leaders and activists, led by Comilla South district Swechchhasebak Dal Convener Syed Meraj Uddin, marching to the Awami League office in Ramghat.
They chanted slogans protesting an attack on a police station in Gopalganj and the arson attack on the residence of BNP MP SM Zilani before setting fire outside the party office.
Another video shows a group of youths marching to Bahar's residence in Munsef Bari. They chanted similar slogans before pouring petrol inside the gate of his personal office on the ground floor and setting it on fire. Papers and wooden materials outside the office were also set ablaze.
Syed Meraj Uddin said the attacks in Gopalganj and on the residence of BNP MP SM Zilani were unacceptable. He said they held an impromptu procession demanding the arrest and exemplary punishment of those involved.
Regarding the fire outside the Awami League office, he said some agitated activists had set fire to tyres and papers out of long-standing resentment, but had no intention of causing major damage. He added that the organisation believed in peaceful and democratic movements.
Kotwali Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Touhidul Anwar said the fire did not last long and no one entered the office. A few youths started the fire from outside using paper, he added.
According to local and party sources, the Awami League offices of Comilla South district and metropolitan units in Ramghat were vandalized and set on fire on August 5, 2024, the day the Awami League government fell.
Bahar's residence and personal office were also attacked, vandalized and looted that day. Since then, family members have not stayed there, except for a night guard.
On the night of February 5, 2025, the residence was attacked again. The attackers tried to break the window grilles, threw bricks and stones, vandalized several parts of the house and set fire to several rooms and the front section after pouring petrol on them.
Attempts were also made to attack the Awami League's metropolitan and south district offices in Ramghat that night. The brick structure in front of the south district office's main gate was demolished.
Former MP AKM Bahauddin Bahar, his daughter and former Comilla City Corporation mayor Dr Tahsin Bahar Suchona, and other family members are currently abroad.

item.title: Winter to be 'warm' for Bangladesh this year
item.description:
Bangladesh is set to experience a gradual onset of winter starting next week, with the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) forecasting a 'warm winter' this year due to the effects of El Nino phase.
"We are expecting a warm winter this year due to El Nino phase," meteorologist Dr Muhammad Abul Kalam Mallik told BSS on Tuesday.
The El Nino phase is the warm part of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a natural climate cycle that swings between warm and cool states in the tropical Pacific Ocean every two to seven years.
Dr Mallik said the winter is expected to start in the country from next week, while fog has already started forming in remote areas across the country.
However, he predicted that the intensity and duration of severe coldwaves would be relatively low this year.
According to the BMD's seasonal outlook, chilly conditions and light morning fog will begin appearing in the northern, northeastern, and central districts by the third week of November. Winter intensity will build steadily through December before reaching its peak in January 2027, with cold weather expected to linger until mid-February.
Meteorologists projected that four to six mild-to-moderate coldwaves would sweep through various parts of the country this season, driving regional minimum temperatures down between 6 and 10°C.
Additionally, two to three severe cold spells could hit the northwest, northeast, and central regions, potentially pushing mercury levels as low as 4 to 6°C.
In the capital, Dhaka, nighttime and early morning temperatures are expected to dip to between 11 and 13°C at the height of the season.
Forecasters also warned of dense late-night and early-morning fog, particularly in the northern and central river basins. The reduced visibility is expected to cause temporary disruptions to road, river, and air transport networks during peak winter weeks.
While broader regional climate models indicate potential warming influences from El Nino patterns this year, weather officials noted that localised cold snaps and sharp overnight temperature drops will still impact daily life and agriculture across the delta nation.
Noting that El Nino is active, Mallik said that during the winter in Bangladesh, night temperatures, on average, remains 14 to 24°C based on stations. "This season, nighttime temperature will be 1 to 2°C higher."
The meteorologist said sea surface temperature, land surface temperature and ocean heat content capacity have increased this year due to global warming, resulting in rise of overall temperature.
"To address this situation, we need localisation of global knowledge and globalisation of local knowledge," he said. According to the three-month climate outlook issued by the BMD on November 1, day and nighttime temperature may remain higher than normal.
Moderate to dense fog may occur at some places across the country, including river basins, from late night to morning, while light to moderate fog may prevail elsewhere over the country.
Due to dense fog, the difference between day and night temperatures may decrease, which may intensify the feeling of cold.
Four to six mild (08-10øC) to moderate (06-08øC) coldwaves may sweep across parts of the country, of which 2-3 may intensify into severe coldwaves (04-06øC) during the winter, the outlook said.

item.title: Most factories reopen in Gazipur after workers' protests
item.description:
Factory operations have resumed across much of Gazipur's industrial belt following a daylong workers' protest on Tuesday, with most factories reopening on Wednesday morning.
Workers joined their shifts at factories in Bhogra Bypass, Naojor, Konabari, Kashimpur, Chandra, Palli Bidyut road, Bhabanipur, Memberbari, Notun Bazar, and Tongi.
Police maintained surveillance across the industrial areas, with no untoward incidents reported until 9:30am.
On Tuesday, garment workers took to the streets demanding a minimum wage and blocked highways. Clashes broke out between workers and police in Bhogra Bypass and the No 2 C&B and Aspada areas of Sreepur.
The clashes involved brick-throwing, tear gas and sound grenades, leaving several police personnel, workers and journalists injured.
Around 70% of garment factories sent workers home early on Tuesday, while 70 factories declared holidays to prevent further unrest.
On Wednesday, security was tightened across the industrial belt, with Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) members deployed alongside police. Traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh and Dhaka-Tangail highways remained normal, and no fresh protests were reported.
Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amzad Hossain said production had resumed at many factories that were closed on Tuesday.
Workers entered factories peacefully and joined production, with no untoward incidents reported since morning, he said.
He added that members of Gazipur Metropolitan Police, district police, industrial police, BGB, the Special Reserve Battalion (SRB) and Ansar would remain deployed to maintain law and order.

item.description:
Ferry services on the Paturia-Daulatdia route were suspended for two hours on Wednesday morning due to dense fog, disrupting river crossings and leaving more than a hundred vehicles stranded at the terminals.
During the suspension, a ferry named Birshreshtha Jahangir remained anchored in the middle of the river, while nine other ferries were berthed at various pontoons at the Paturia and Daulatdia terminals.
BIWTC Deputy General Manager (DGM) Abdus Salam said ferry operations were suspended at 6:00am on Wednesday as dense fog intensified, posing a risk of maritime accidents.
The suspension continued for two hours, with ferry services resuming around 8:00am as visibility improved and the fog began to clear.
Meanwhile, ferry services on the Aricha-Kazirhat route were also suspended for an hour from 6m due to dense fog.

The bus, belonging to Three Star Paribahan, was parked beside the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway near a garage owned by Md Latif when two youths on a motorcycle set it ablaze and fled.
Local residents rushed to the spot and extinguished the fire, which damaged several parts of the bus.
No casualties were reported.
The bus was owned by Lokman Mamun, a resident of Demra's Staff Quarter area, and was used to transport employees of various offices.
Siddhirganj Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Emdadul Haque said police were working to identify those responsible. Further details would be shared after the investigation.

item.title: Hasan, Taskin strike before rain washes out two sessions on Day 3
item.description:
Bangladesh fought back with three wickets in the opening session before persistent rain and thunderstorms forced an early end to the third day of the first Test against South Africa at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg on Tuesday.
South Africa reached 386-7 in 90 overs at stumps, trailing Bangladesh's first-innings total of 400 by just 14 runs, with only one session of play possible due to adverse weather conditions.
Resuming the day at 287-4, the hosts looked well placed to take control of the contest as captain Temba Bavuma and Ryan Rickelton continued their resistance. The pair added valuable runs before Bavuma was forced to retire hurt on 49 due to muscle cramps, with South Africa on 358-4.
Bangladesh, however, made the most of the second new ball to turn the momentum around. Taskin Ahmed struck twice in quick succession, first dismissing Wiaan Mulder for a duck before removing Marco Jansen for eight.
Hasan Mahmud then strengthened Bangladesh's position by dismissing Simon Harmer, leaving South Africa seven wickets down and still behind.
Rickelton remained unbeaten on 56 at the interval, while Kagiso Rabada was not out on five. Hasan was Bangladesh's most successful bowler, finishing with figures of 4-72, while Taskin claimed 2-88.
Bangladesh had earlier posted a formidable 400 in their first innings, built around Liton Das's century. The wicketkeeper-batter's innings provided the foundation for the visitors to put up a challenging total in the opening innings.
The second session was completely washed out as a severe thunderstorm, accompanied by heavy rain and hail, swept across Johannesburg. Although the rain briefly eased, persistent lightning, dark skies and further showers prevented the players from returning to the field after lunch.
There was little improvement in conditions ahead of the scheduled final session, with the ground remaining covered as thunder and lightning continued in the area. With no prospect of a resumption, the umpires eventually called stumps at around 3:55pm local time.
The weather interruption means South Africa will resume on the fourth morning needing just 14 runs to erase Bangladesh's first-innings advantage, with three wickets remaining. Rickelton's presence at the crease gives the hosts a chance to move ahead, while Bangladesh will look to wrap up the innings quickly and secure a potentially crucial first-innings lead.
Further rain is also forecast for the fourth day, raising the possibility of more interruptions in a match that remains finely balanced.

Arson, attacks beyond Dhaka fuel fears of fresh political unrest
item.description:
Political violence and sabotage spread beyond Dhaka on Tuesday, with attacks on a police station and a BNP lawmaker’s home in Gopalganj, and a road blockade and arson in Faridpur that left a Krishak Dal leader dead.
Several buses were also set on fire and crude bombs exploded at different locations in the capital. The circulation of an alleged audio clip featuring provocative remarks by a former minister now abroad has further fuelled political tension, raising fears of fresh unrest.
The country has been witnessing heightened political tensions for more than a month, with reports of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson almost daily.
In the audio clip circulated on social media on Tuesday, a voice is heard calling for two or three houses to be set on fire in every union and suggesting assault and killing if necessary. The remarks appear to target the ruling BNP and the National Citizen Party (NCP). The authenticity of the recording has not been established.
Around 9pm on Tuesday, activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League allegedly blocked the Dhaka-Barisal highway in Pukuria, Bhanga, Faridpur, and set fire to three motorcycles. Krishak Dal leader Raju Molla died after suffering severe burns.
Earlier, around 8:30pm, unidentified people set fire to the former residence of former Liberation War Affairs minister AKM Mozammel Haque in Gazipur. In Gopalganj, Awami League and Chhatra League activists allegedly vandalised and set fire to the home of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani, representing Gopalganj-3.
Attackers also set fire to Tungipara Police Station after making announcements over mosque loudspeakers. Clashes broke out between police and the attackers, leaving several police personnel injured. Earlier in the day, a group chanting slogans in support of the Awami League allegedly attacked and vandalised a BNP leader’s business establishment in Chittagong’s Khatunganj.
The incidents have prompted questions about whether the country is heading towards another period of political instability and how the ruling BNP and the NCP, which emerged from the July uprising, will respond.
Leaders from both parties said they primarily planned to keep their activists engaged in regular political programmes in December. They said the administration should deal with attempts to create disorder, while the parties would consider political programmes depending on developments.
Political leaders and analysts have warned that a failure by political parties to act responsibly could disrupt the democratic process and create an anarchic situation. They have urged all sides to exercise restraint.
Former Communist Party of Bangladesh general secretary Ruhin Hossain Prince said any provocative remarks encouraging violence were unacceptable, if the audio clip was genuine. However, he cautioned against political parties taking matters into their own hands, saying law enforcement agencies should handle attempts at sabotage.
Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque also condemned any alleged incitement to violence. He said the BNP and NCP could organise constructive programmes to prevent sabotage, but all parties must remain tolerant to preserve a healthy political environment.
Political analyst and writer Mahiuddin Ahmed said it was too early to determine whether the current situation would lead to further clashes.
The NCP has not announced any special programme to counter the activities of any particular political group in December. Its leaders said the party would focus on its scheduled programmes, including Victory Day celebrations, rather than taking to the streets in response to the actions of others.
NCP Joint Convener and Political Council member Sarwar Tushar said maintaining law and order was the administration’s responsibility, not the party’s.
He said the public would resist those attempting to create disorder if they crossed the limits.
The BNP has already instructed its leaders and activists to remain active alongside the administration to counter attempts to destabilise the country.
Acting BNP Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said on Sunday that party activists and those of its associate organisations would remain active in neighbourhoods to prevent sabotage.
A BNP joint secretary general, speaking on condition of anonymity, said party activists were holding meetings and rallies across the country and informing the administration about suspected acts of sabotage.
BNP Vice-Chairman Shamsuzzaman Dudu said the administration was responsible for controlling sabotage, but the party would remain active to protect public safety and maintain a normal political environment.
He said the party had planned peaceful programmes around Victory Day and the death anniversary of former prime minister Khaleda Zia in December, while maintaining a firm stance against violence.
Speaking at a programme at Rajshahi University on Tuesday, Rizvi said attempts were being made to return to power through crude bomb blasts, arson attacks on buses and attacks on police boxes. However, he said such incidents would not derail the country's democratic journey.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed addressed the attack on Tungipara Police Station, urging residents of Gopalganj not to fall for provocations allegedly coming from across the border.
He said the government had refrained from ordering a forceful response despite having police, Border Guard Bangladesh and other security personnel deployed near the area, as it wanted to avoid casualties.
The minister warned that those involved in the attack on the police station, assaults on law enforcement personnel, arson and acts of sabotage would be identified through video footage, audio recordings and photographs and brought to justice.

item.title: Awami League activists torch police station, BNP MP’s house in Gopalganj
item.description:
Activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations allegedly stormed Tungipara Police Station in Gopalganj on Tuesday evening, vandalised the premises, set fire to police vehicles and subsequently torched the residence of BNP lawmaker SM Jilani, triggering widespread panic and fresh concerns over the deteriorating security situation.
The violence erupted around 7:30pm after police detained several suspected Chhatra League activists, prompting hundreds of Awami League supporters to surround the police station and demand their release.
According to police and local witnesses, the protesters, many carrying sticks, overwhelmed police resistance, entered the station compound and set fire to vehicles and parts of the premises.
Witnesses also reported that the attackers freed the detained activists, although police had not independently confirmed their escape.
Police reportedly fired tear gas shells, rubber bullets and sound grenades to disperse the crowd, leading to clashes and chases.
Several people were reportedly injured, but their number and condition could not immediately be confirmed.
A short while later, another group of alleged Chhatra League activists attacked and set fire to the house of SM Jilani, the BNP lawmaker representing Gopalganj-3, comprising Tungipara and Kotalipara.
Tungipara Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mohammad Didarul Alam confirmed the attack on the lawmaker’s residence.
Witnesses said the attackers chanted slogans supporting the Awami League and Sheikh Hasina during the violence.
According to local sources, the confrontation began after police detained several Chhatra League activists near the upazila parishad while they were having tea.
The detainees were taken to Tungipara Police Station, prompting supporters to mobilise through loudspeaker announcements and gather outside the facility.
As the crowd grew, protesters attempted to enter the police station, leading to clashes with law enforcement personnel.
Police reportedly fired several rounds and used crowd-control equipment before retreating amid the confrontation.
Videos circulating on Facebook appeared to show at least three vehicles burning inside the station compound, while protesters shouted slogans and vandalised property.
In one Facebook Live broadcast, an individual identified as HM Rubel Farazi was heard threatening to set the police station on fire.
The authenticity and full circumstances of the footage could not immediately be independently verified.
Police Headquarters spokesperson Kamarum Munira confirmed around 9:10pm that Tungipara Police Station had been attacked and set on fire.
She said police had also received reports of vehicles being torched.
Earlier, Police Headquarters DIG (Crime and Operations) Mohammed Abu Sufian said authorities were gathering information after receiving reports that the station had been surrounded.
Eskandar Sheikh, acting station officer of Tungipara Fire Service, said firefighters had received reports of fires near the police station, Chourangi intersection and Bashbaria.
However, fire crews were unable to reach the affected locations because of security concerns.
He said firefighters would proceed once adequate protection was provided by law enforcement agencies.
Meanwhile, Awami League supporters reportedly erected barricades at Khalek Bazar, Patgati intersection, Barni and other points along roads connecting Gopalganj and Tungipara, disrupting traffic.
The latest attacks followed several days of unrest in Gopalganj, where activities-banned Awami League supporters staged armed processions, vandalised public property and reopened party offices.
Authorities had deployed additional security personnel and transferred the district’s deputy commissioner, superintendent of police and three officers-in-charge following Sunday’s violence.

item.title: Krishak Dal leader burnt to death during Awami Leaue blockade in Faridpur
item.description:
A local Krishak Dal leader died after being severely burned when three motorcycles were set on fire during a road blockade on the Dhaka-Barisal highway in Faridpur’s Bhanga Upazila on Tuesday night.
The incident took place around 9pm in the Pukuria area. The deceased, Raju Molla, was the joint organising secretary of Bhanga Upazila Krishak Dal and the son of Muktar Molla of Bakpura village.
Bhanga Upazila BNP President Khandaker Iqbal Hossain Selim alleged that activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League blocked the road, set fire to several motorcycles and attacked Raju before setting him on fire.
According to eyewitnesses and local sources, Raju sustained critical burn injuries and was taken to Bhanga Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared him dead.
Health complex physician Tanzirul Islam Mamun said Raju was brought to the hospital around 9:30pm. Much of his body below the waist had been burned, he added.
Following the blockade and arson, local BNP activists went to the scene and, with police assistance, cleared the road and restored traffic. They also staged an immediate protest over Raju’s death.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Special Branch) Raihan Gafur said police had brought the situation under control after reaching the scene. Police were working to identify those involved, he added.

item.title: Sayeed Khokon placed on 7-day remand in teenager murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) mayor Sayeed Khokon on a seven-day remand for questioning in a case filed over the murder of teenager Abdul Motaleb in the capital’s Dhanmondi area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mehedi Hasan passed the order on Tuesday, following a petition filed by the investigation officer.
Inspector Sujan Haque of the Detective Branch (DB) police’s Ramna Zonal Team, who is investigating the case, had sought a 10-day remand for Khokon.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi argued in favour of the remand on behalf of the state, while senior lawyer Abu Sayeed Sagor, representing Khokon, opposed the plea and sought his bail.
According to the case statement, Motaleb was shot dead on August 4, 2024 while taking part in a procession near Zigatola Bus Stand during the July uprising.
On August 26, 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government, his father Abdul Matin filed a murder case with Dhanmondi Police Station.
The case names 176 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader. Khokon is listed as the 29th accused in the FIR.
Khokon, son of former undivided Dhaka City Corporation mayor Mohammad Hanif, was elected DSCC mayor in 2015. He was denied the Awami League's nomination in the subsequent mayoral election.
He later contested the 12th parliamentary election with the party's nomination and was elected MP from the Dhaka-6 constituency.
He was detained from a residence in Baridhara around 7am on Tuesday. SRB later handed him over to the Detective Branch (DB) of police.
