item.title: Board chief: New garment wages to take effect from Dec 1, regardless of announcement date
item.description:
New wages for garment workers will take effect from December 1, regardless of when they are officially announced, Minimum Wage Board Chairman Syed Azad Subhani said on Tuesday.
He urged workers not to be misled by rumours, misinformation or fake notices regarding the wage announcement and called on them to avoid creating disorder.
He made the remarks at a briefing at the Minimum Wage Board office in Segunbagicha in the capital.
Subhani said the board's scheduled meeting on Monday was postponed after one of its representatives fell ill. The meeting will now be held on November 23.
Reiterating the implementation timeline, he said the new minimum wages would come into effect from December 1, irrespective of the announcement date.
The government formed a six-member Minimum Wage Board for garment workers on November 1. A tripartite emergency meeting involving representatives of workers, employers and the government was also held on the same day.
Despite these initiatives, workers' protests have continued in several areas. In response, the government has stepped up security in industrial zones, deploying police, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and Armed Police Battalion (APBn) personnel.

item.title: Wife claims physically disabled man framed in Jessore court blast case
item.description:
A man accused in a case filed over a cocktail explosion on the Jessore court premises is physically unfit and unable to walk properly, his wife has claimed, alleging that he was implicated in the case to harass him despite having no involvement in political activities.
Rani Begum made the allegations at a press conference at Press Club Jessore around noon on Tuesday, where she read out a written statement on behalf of her husband, Jahidul Islam Tanvir.
She called for an impartial investigation into the incident, consideration of her husband's physical condition and medical needs, and security for their family.
According to the written statement, Tanvir runs a small fish business beside the Chanchra-Bablatala road to support his family and has no affiliation with any political party.
Rani alleged that after August 5, 2025, members of a force detained and beat her husband in front of their home over an incident. He and his mother were later taken to a police station but were released as no specific evidence was found against him.
She said Tanvir fell into a ditch around 1:30am on October 14 while heading out for his fish business, tearing the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) in his left leg. Following medical advice, he has been unable to move around normally.
The family has also been unable to arrange the necessary treatment due to financial constraints, she added.
However, Tanvir was named among 21 accused in a case filed over the cocktail explosions on theJessore court premises on November 12.
Questioning how a person unable to stand properly could have been involved in the incident, Rani demanded an impartial investigation into the allegations against her husband.
She said Tanvir is the family's sole breadwinner and that they have two sons. His illness, mounting medical expenses and the case have plunged the family into uncertainty.
Those present at the press conference included Tanvir's mother, Jesmin Sultana; aunt, Rekha Begum; another relative, Oheda Begum; neighbour Lamia Sultana; and his seven-year-old son, Taiyan Rahman.
The family also urged the authorities to identify the actual perpetrators and ensure their safety.
Meanwhile, police sources said Tanvir was arrested in connection with a drug-related case filed at a police station in 2023.

Witnesses said activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League marched to the police station around 7:30pm, vandalised the premises and set fire to parts of the building. Police came under attack while trying to bring the situation under control, triggering clashes and chases between the two sides.
According to police, witnesses and local sources, the activists had surrounded the police station to free several suspects arrested over alleged sabotage incidents across the town on Sunday.
When police resisted, clashes broke out, and officers reportedly fired several rounds. Police later retreated following a chase, allowing the attackers to enter the station, vandalise it and set fire to several police vehicles.
A short while later, Chhatra League activists allegedly set fire to Jilani’s house while chanting “Joy Bangla”.
The successive demonstrations, attacks and fires spread panic across the area.

item.title: Labour unrest returns to Savar-Ashulia, 80 factories declare holiday
item.description:
Around 80 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared general holidays on Tuesday amid renewed labour unrest, while eight factories remained indefinitely closed under the Bangladesh Labour Act as workers blocked roads and clashed with police at several locations.
The unrest erupted after two consecutive days of relative calm in the industrial belt, with workers demanding an increase in minimum wages and raising other workplace-related demands. Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse protesters and restore order.
At around 9:30am, workers of Standard Group gathered on the road at Padmar Mor in Hemayetpur, Savar, instead of joining work. They dumped industrial waste on the road and set it on fire.
When police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel attempted to clear the road, clashes broke out. Workers threw bricks at law enforcement personnel, prompting police to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them.
Around 11am, workers from AKH and several other garment factories took to the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in the Rajfulbaria area of Savar, triggering severe traffic congestion on both sides of the highway.
Police later dispersed the workers, and traffic resumed around 1pm.
Asaduzzaman Noor, officer-in-charge of Savar Highway Police Station, said traffic movement had come to a halt after workers occupied the highway. It returned to normal after they left the road.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Meanwhile, workers initially entered factories in the Ashulia industrial belt in the morning, but unrest began to emerge as the day progressed.
Workers of The Rose factory in Jamgora punched in but did not join work, opting instead for a work stoppage. The factory authorities subsequently declared a holiday citing security concerns.
Workers of Radiance Fashion and Radiance Jeans in the Khejurbagan area also stopped work and took to the streets after being released from their factories. Clashes and chases between police and workers followed. Traffic returned to normal after police brought the situation under control.
Before noon, at least seven factories, including those of Maxtex and Mondol Group in Matborbari, Narsinghpur and surrounding areas, declared general holidays.
According to Industrial Police, eight factories in Savar and Ashulia remain indefinitely closed under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act.
Although most factories that had previously been shut reopened in phases, fresh unrest emerged at several facilities. Meanwhile, around 80 factories in the industrial belt declared general holidays amid labour unrest and security concerns.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police of Industrial Police-1, said the situation had been relatively normal on Tuesday morning compared with the previous two days, and several previously closed factories had resumed operations.
However, workers at several factories later refused to join work and attempted to stage work stoppages and block roads.
To prevent disorder and ensure the safety of factories and the general public, factory authorities were compelled to declare holidays at some facilities, he said.
Additional police personnel have been deployed across the industrial belt to maintain security and ensure normal traffic movement on highways, Bhuiyan added.
Police and BGB remain on alert to prevent further untoward incidents.
Although the situation was under control at the time of reporting, law enforcement agencies maintained heightened surveillance across the industrial belt amid concerns over possible renewed tensions.

item.title: Bangladesh emerges as 33rd nuclear power nation: Faqir Mahbub
item.description:
Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam on Tuesday said Bangladesh has emerged as the world's 33rd nuclear power country through the successful trial connection of electricity from the first unit of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant (RNPP) to the national grid, describing it as "very happy news for the entire nation".
Talking to journalists in front of the plant in Ishwardi in Pabna after the successful trial connection, the minister announced the "historic achievement".
Bangladesh's nuclear power plant began trial power supply Tuesday afternoon after successfully completing synchronisation with the national grid, said a ministry press release.
The minister said electricity generated at Rooppur, Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant, was connected to the national grid on a trial basis after a long wait, continuous technical activities and complex tests at various stages.
Power supply of 350 megawatts from the first unit to the national grid began for the first time at 3pm on Tuesday in the presence of Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam.
Briefing journalists on the current status of the trial supply, he said the results were "very satisfactory". The supply was later reduced and held steady at 300 megawatts to maintain grid stability.
Referring to the observations of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the minister said its delegation is very satisfied with the overall progress and safety arrangements of the project, which made it possible to carry out Tuesday’s successful grid synchronisation test.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman extended congratulations to all concerned on the "extraordinary success", while the minister expressed gratitude to the people of the country.
He described it as an important milestone in Rooppur's power generation and grid connection activities.
Prime Minister's Adviser on Science and Technology Rehan Asif Asad, Science and Technology Ministry Secretary Md Anwar Hossain, RNPP Construction Project Director Dr Md Kabir Hossain and Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Limited (NPCBL) Managing Director Dr Zahedul Hasan, among others, were present during the briefing.
Kabir Hossain said that, as per the set plan, electricity generated under the initial trial connection will be supplied to the national grid for about eight to 10 hours.
During this time, important technical tests will be carried out, including observation of the performance and stability of the plant's turbine, generator and the operating system integrated with the grid, he added.
The plant will later be disconnected from the national grid for various technical tests. After a break of about 28 hours, it will be reconnected to the grid for four to six hours to complete the necessary technical and operational tests, he added.
He said the performance of the plant's various systems, the turbine and generator, and coordination with the national grid will be closely checked at every stage of the tests.
Once the results of all technical tests are satisfactory and all work set for this stage is completed, approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) will be required for the next trial operation.
Subject to BAERA's approval, the plant will be connected to the national grid again on a trial operation basis and the next phase of power supply will be advanced, Kabir said.
Under the agreement with the Russian contractor, commercial power supply from the first unit at full capacity will begin on a permanent basis after the 10-month trial operation is completed, he said.
The Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission will then take provisional takeover of the first unit from the Russian contractor. Later, NPCBL will begin operations as the operating organisation through a government gazette notification.
Each of the two units of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts, giving the plant a total capacity of 2,400 megawatts. The plant is expected to make an important contribution to meeting the country's growing power demand, ensuring energy security and sustainable power generation.
The trial grid connection of the plant is a historic step in the progress of Bangladesh's power and energy sector, the release said.
With this, Bangladesh has moved one step further in nuclear technology-based power generation.

item.title: Police seek 10-day remand for ex-DSCC mayor Sayeed Khokon in teen murder case
item.description:
Police have sought a 10-day remand for former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) mayor Sayeed Khokon in a murder case filed over the killing of teenager Abdul Motaleb in the capital’s Dhanmondi area. Deputy Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Prosecution Division, Mohiuddin Mahmud Sohel, confirmed the remand application on Tuesday.
He said the hearing would be held at the court of Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mehedi Hasan.
Inspector Sujan Haque of the Ramna Zonal Team, who is also the investigation officer in the case, filed the remand petition.
According to the case statement, Motaleb was shot dead on August 4, 2024 while taking part in a procession near Zigatola Bus Stand during the July uprising.
On August 26, 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government, his father Abdul Matin filed a murder case with Dhanmondi Police Station.
The case names 176 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former road transport and bridges minister Obaidul Quader. Khokon is listed as the 29th accused in the FIR.
Khokon, son of former undivided Dhaka City Corporation mayor Mohammad Hanif, was elected DSCC mayor in 2015. He was denied the Awami League's nomination in the subsequent mayoral election.
He later contested the 12th parliamentary election with the party's nomination and was elected MP from the Dhaka-6 constituency.
He was detained from a residence in Baridhara around 7am on Tuesday. SRB later handed him over to the Detective Branch (DB) of police.

item.title: BNP MP Osman Faruk resigns citing illness
item.description:
Dr Mohammad Osman Faruk, the BNP lawmaker elected from Kishoreganj-3, has resigned from parliament, citing physical illness.
He sent his resignation letter by email to Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, who informed parliament of the decision and declared the seat vacant.
The Speaker announced the resignation at the start of Tuesday’s sitting on the seventh day of the fourth session of the 13th parliament, which began at 4:15pm.
According to sources close to Osman Faruk, he has been staying in the United States for some time. He cited physical illness in his resignation letter. He was also absent from the presidential election on August 20, as he was in the US at the time.
Party sources said health complications prompted his decision to resign.
Reading out the resignation notice in parliament, the speaker said Osman Faruk, elected from constituency No 164 (Kishoreganj-3), had submitted a signed resignation letter, effective from November 14.
The speaker received it on November 15 and accepted it after finding it compliant with parliamentary rules.
Citing Article 67(2) of the Constitution, the speaker said the seat became vacant upon receipt of the resignation letter.
“Accordingly, the Kishoreganj-3 seat became vacant from the morning of November 15. The House is hereby informed of the vacancy under Article 67(2) of the Constitution of Bangladesh and Rule 178(3) of the Rules of Procedure of Parliament,” he said.

item.title: Zahed: Govt monitoring public servants with Awami League links
item.description:
The government is keeping public servants who are politically involved with the Awami League under the highest level of surveillance, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Dr Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday, warning that political affiliation while holding public office is a serious concern.
"Many people are or were associated with the Awami League because the party was in power. That is not a problem. They are public servants and are performing their duties. But if they remain politically affiliated while holding public office, that is a very serious matter," he said.
The adviser made the remarks while speaking at a press briefing on the progress of various government activities at the Secretariat.
Noting that the government had its own surveillance and intelligence-gathering mechanisms, Zahed declined to disclose details, citing matters related to state security.
Talking about Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, the adviser said it will be expired on December 12, adding that he had no new information on the matter at the moment.
However, Bangladesh had completed the necessary preparations and would inform the media in due course about its expectations and approach to the issue, he said.
Asked about the possibility of the prime minister visiting India, he said there was no such possibility at present.
He also clarified that the prime minister's visit was not directly linked to discussions or the finalisation of the treaty.
Regarding the latest review of 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding (MoUs) between Bangladesh and India, the adviser said he did not have sufficient information at the moment.
He said the government would try to provide an update at the next press briefing.
Regarding efforts to bring former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back from India, Zahed said the government's position was clear that is Bangladesh wanted her extradition.
Bangladesh had formally requested her extradition under the existing treaty between the two countries, he said.
Asked whether India had imposed any conditions or exerted pressure in this regard, the adviser said he did not believe the Indian government would set any conditions.

item.title: Rooppur nuclear plant supplies 350MW to national grid on trial basis
item.description:
The first unit of Bangladesh’s maiden nuclear power plant at Rooppur has begun supplying 350 megawatts (MW) of electricity to the national grid on a trial basis.
The initial supply began at 3pm on Tuesday in the presence of Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam, the Power Division said in a statement.
The development marks a major milestone following years of work, technical preparations and a series of complex tests to bring the plant into operation.
According to the Power Division, the initial trial connection will last around 8-10 hours, during which the performance and stability of the plant’s turbine, generator and integrated systems connected to the national grid will be assessed.
The plant will then be disconnected from the national grid for further technical tests. After a break of around 28 hours, it will be reconnected for another 4-6 hours to complete the necessary technical and operational assessments.
Relevant sources said the performance of various plant systems, including the turbine and generator, as well as their coordination with the national grid, would be closely monitored at every stage.
Once all tests yield satisfactory results and the scheduled activities for this phase are completed, the plant will require approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) to proceed to the next phase of trial operation.
Subject to regulatory approval, the plant will again be connected to the national grid on a trial basis to continue electricity supply.
Under the agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit will undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning permanent commercial electricity supply at full capacity.
Following the successful completion of the trial period, the first unit will be provisionally handed over by the Russian contractor to the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission.
The Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Limited (NPCBL) will subsequently begin operating the plant as its designated operating organisation following a government gazette notification.
The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has two units, each with a generation capacity of 1,200MW, giving it a combined capacity of 2,400MW.
The plant is expected to play a significant role in meeting the country's growing electricity demand, strengthening energy security and ensuring a sustainable power supply.

item.title: Dengue: 5 more die, 1,537 hospitalised in 24hrs
item.description:
Five people died of dengue and 1,537 new patients were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours till Tuesday morning.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 507 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the new deaths, five were recorded in Dhaka division.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 165,644 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 159,528 have recovered.
Currently, 5,609 patients are receiving treatment at different hospitals across the country.

item.title: Workers' strike halts container handling at Chittagong Port
item.description:
Loading and unloading operations at several container terminals of Chittagong port came to a halt on Tuesday as workers of controversial operator Saif Powertec went on a work stoppage demanding payment of outstanding wages, bonuses and other benefits.
More than 500 workers went on work abstention in the morning at the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT), Chittagong Container Terminal (CCT) and other terminals, disrupting cargo handling activities at the port.
The workers said they had been demanding payment of several months' outstanding wages and other dues, but Saif Powertec authorities had taken no effective steps despite being given several ultimatums.
Their five-point demand includes payment of arrear salaries, bonuses, gratuities, Covid-period bonuses, compensation for working on public holidays and bonuses for the two Eid festivals, among other financial benefits.
The workers said operations had been suspended at seven berths, where seven cargo vessels were waiting.
They said the port authorities had informed them of plans to hold discussions, but no solution had yet been reached.
The agitating workers said they were compelled to go on strike as their demands had remained unaddressed for a long time.
Secretary of Chittagong Port, Syed Refayet Hamim, said the workers went on work abstention from 8am.
He expressed hope that the workers would withdraw the program following discussions with them.
Meanwhile, Chittagong Dry Dock Limited (CDDL) operates NCT, while workers of Saif Powertec are engaged in its operations.
DP World is expected to take over the operation of NCT soon, while Saif Powertec's contract to operate CCT is nearing its end.

item.title: Police, administration face growing scrutiny amid calls for accountability
item.description:
The transfer of five senior officials in Gopalganj, the arrest of a police superintendent in Chittagong, the relocation of more than 100 police personnel from Cox’s Bazar and the withdrawal of Chuadanga Deputy Commissioner Lutfun Nahar have brought renewed attention to oversight and accountability in the police and civil administration.
The developments have also raised questions about whether the government is pursuing a broader drive to address misconduct, negligence and alleged political or criminal links within state institutions.
In Gopalganj, the deputy commissioner and superintendent of police were transferred following a series of violent incidents, while the officers-in-charge of three police stations were also moved. In Chittagong, a police officer holding the rank of superintendent was arrested on charges of sedition and incitement to conspire against the state.
Officials and analysts say the transfers and investigations should not automatically be treated as disciplinary action, as administrative postings, departmental inquiries and criminal proceedings have different legal implications.
Violence in Gopalganj since November 10 has included protests, road blockades, attacks on vehicles, vandalism and arson. Fresh tensions erupted on Sunday surrounding a procession by leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations. Homes, party offices and businesses belonging to BNP leaders were attacked. Ten platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh were deployed on Monday.
On Sunday, DC Md Arif-uz-Zaman was withdrawn and attached to the Ministry of Public Administration. He was replaced by Habiganj DC GM Sarfaraz. Gopalganj SP Md Habibullah was transferred to Feni, while Feni SP Pratyush Kumar Majumder was posted to Gopalganj. The OCs of Tungipara, Kotalipara and Kashiani police stations were also transferred to Kishoreganj.
The changes have prompted questions about whether intelligence warnings were available before the violence and whether the administration and police were adequately coordinated in responding to it.
At a November 10 meeting with police superintendents from all 64 districts and other senior officials, Inspector General of Police Ali Hossain Fakir ordered increased intelligence surveillance, patrols and searches, with particular attention to Gopalganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur and Faridpur.
Police headquarters said 27 locations saw cocktail explosions and 19 buses were set on fire between November 7 and 9. Eleven cases were filed and 29 people arrested. The IGP also stressed that innocent people should not be harassed in the name of operations.
In Chittagong, Mohammad Jahangir Alam, deputy commandant of the Range Reserve Force, was arrested over allegations of sedition and incitement to conspire against the state. Police said an investigation began over two messages on his mobile phone. His official and personal phones were seized on November 10, and a court later granted a four-day remand.
In Cox’s Bazar, 100 police personnel were transferred elsewhere over 10 months, from December to September, amid allegations of links between police members and drug traders. They included 27 sub-inspectors, 41 assistant sub-inspectors and 32 constables.
Additional IGP Khandaker Rafiqul Islam said that police intelligence units routinely monitor members of the force to prevent misconduct and disciplinary violations. He described the recent incidents as isolated and said there was no reason for concern.
At an emergency meeting of secretaries on November 12, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani called for faster administrative work. Sources said the meeting also discussed whether some officials were slowing down their work amid uncertainty over the political situation.
Chuadanga DC and District Magistrate Lutfun Nahar was withdrawn on Sunday, eight days after controversy over a government programme marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day and her speech at the event. Md Alamgir Kabir was appointed as her replacement.
Experts say accountability measures are necessary but must be based on specific evidence. Dr Touhidul Haque, an associate professor at the University of Dhaka’s Institute of Social Welfare and Research and a crime analyst, said transfers alone cannot resolve institutional weaknesses.
He stressed the need for impartial investigations, legal action against officials found involved in wrongdoing and a safe working environment for honest and competent officers. Without transparency and due process, he warned, excessive surveillance could deepen fear, uncertainty and mistrust within the administration.

item.title: Normalcy returns to Gopalganj after days of unrest
item.description:
Life and the law and order situation in Gopalganj has gradually returned to normal following days of violence and unrest, with no fresh incidents reported in the town on Tuesday.
From morning until afternoon, no activists of the banned Awami League were seen on the streets, while residents and businesses resumed their daily activities amid tight security.
Law enforcement personnel maintained a visible presence across the town, with patrols stepped up at key intersections, important installations and crowded public areas.
According to law enforcement sources, 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), around 2,000 police personnel, including members of the Rapid Action Battalion (RRF) and Armed Police Battalion (APBn), and eight platoons of Ansar Battalion have been deployed across the district to maintain law and order.
BGB personnel were patrolling key intersections and installations in armoured personnel carriers (APCs), equipped with body-worn cameras. Drones were also being used to monitor the situation on the ground.
A visit to the town found shops and business establishments reopening, with more people returning to the streets. Shopping centres were open, while long-distance buses and inter-district public transport services were operating normally.
Traffic movement was also normal along the 67-kilometre stretch of the Dhaka-Khulna highway and other roads across the district. No untoward incidents were reported on these routes.
Since morning, police personnel were seen deployed at key locations, including Ghonapara intersection, LGED intersection, Bedgram, Police Lines intersection, Jugoshikha intersection, the district judge's court, the deputy commissioner's residence and Swarnakali High School.
BGB armoured personnel carriers were also patrolling the Gopalganj-Patgati road, the area outside the deputy commissioner's office and the court premises.
The BGB media department said 10 platoons of its personnel had been deployed at key locations across the district to maintain law and order and ensure public safety.
The personnel are carrying out their duties in coordination with the local administration and police.
The BGB headquarters' monitoring cell is also maintaining technology-based surveillance to closely monitor the situation and coordinate field operations.
Live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and improvised devices is being monitored round the clock, the department said.
Eight platoons of Ansar Battalion personnel have also been deployed in the district to prevent sabotage and disorder surrounding the lockdown programme announced by the banned Awami League.
Deputy Director General of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Force's Dhaka Range Asaduzzaman Gani disclosed the information at an emergency press conference at the Bedgram Ansar Battalion camp in Gopalganj at 11am on Tuesday.
He said lethal weapons and live ammunition would not be used under any circumstances to deal with sabotage or disorder.
On November 15, activists of the banned Awami League staged demonstrations and carried out several incidents of vandalism and arson in Gopalganj.
Many of them were seen carrying locally made weapons, including poles, oars, sticks, machetes, Chinese axes, spears and lances.
During the demonstrations, a police armoured vehicle and a police box were vandalised. The activists also damaged the nameplates of the July Memorial and Hadi Chattar.
That evening, the house of Imdadul Haque Mollah, president of Tungipara municipal BNP, several shops and the upazila Jubo Dal office were vandalised and set on fire.
A Grameen Bank office in Tungipara was also vandalised and torched later that night.
In the latest incident, activists of the banned Awami League brought out a procession in Tungipara at around 11am on Monday, broke the lock of their party office and held a meeting there.

item.title: UN: All acts of violence in Bangladesh should be thoroughly investigated
item.description:
Highlighting the importance of peaceful protests, the United Nations (UN) has said that all acts of violence should be thoroughly investigated by the authorities in Bangladesh.
“Well, we believe that all acts of violence should be thoroughly investigated by the national authorities,” Deputy Spokesman for the UN Secretary-General Farhan Haq told reporters during a regular briefing in New York on Monday.
He made the remarks in response to a question from a Bangladeshi journalist seeking the UN’s comments on attacks on Grameen Bank branches.
“But certainly, for our part, we believe, of course, that protesters have the right to peaceful protest, but we emphasise that it must be peaceful protest,” Haq said.
The management of Grameen Bank expressed its deep concern and strongly condemned the recent “series of arson attacks, acts of vandalism, and sabotage” targeting various branches of the institution, an organization dedicated to the financial empowerment of the country’s poor and marginalized populations.
According to reports, between November 10 and Monday, a total of 20 Grameen Bank branches across various regions, including Sherpur, Cox’s Bazar, Madaripur, Dinajpur, Naogaon, Patuakhali, Noakhali, Chittagong, Pabna, Nilphamari, Netrokona, Kishoreganj, Gazipur, Sylhet, Gopalganj, and Rangpur, were subjected to arson or attempted arson, said the bank in a statement.
The bank sincerely hoped that the relevant authorities will conduct a thorough investigation into these incidents, identify those responsible, take appropriate legal action, and continue to ensure the safety of its branches, staff, and members across the country.
Nobel Laureate Dr Muhammad Yunus, who served as the chief adviser of the interim government, is the bank's founder.

item.title: Nurul Afser joins Southeast Bank as director
item.description:
Md Nurul Afser has recently joined the board of directors of Southeast Bank PLC as a shareholder director.
He is a businessman & entrepreneur who is the founder director of Electro Mart Ltd. (a business house promoting electronics and home appliances in Bangladesh) and Trade International Industries Ltd. (a manufacturing plant for electronics and home appliances).
Md Afser, who is presently holding the position of deputy managing director of both the companies, is a person with an unwavering dedication to innovation, relentless drive and an insatiable thirst for success.
He is the member of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI).
Md Nurul Afser is an MBA with his exceptional business acumen, unwavering determination and commitment novelty, he has earned a reputation as the successful entrepreneur in the field of electronics & home appliances industry in Bangladesh.
In his 33 years of business journey, he has played a significant role in leading & setting up the different business houses and institutions by his own initiatives and dynamic leadership.

item.title: Hasnat calls India ‘largest house of cross-border terrorists’
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Senior Joint Convener and lawmaker Hasnat Abdullah on Tuesday described India as the “largest house of cross-border terrorists”, accusing it of providing shelter and support to leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League and Chhatra League, who were attempting to create instability in Bangladesh.
“India is the largest house of cross-border terrorists. Those who threaten Bangladesh's sovereignty and have killed people in this country are being provided shelter there,” he said.
Hasnat also urged the government to question India over its alleged role and seek a clear explanation about its position, saying the activities posed a direct challenge to the country's sovereignty.
He alleged that people involved in activities against Bangladesh were operating from Indian territory, carrying out violence in the country and returning to India, while New Delhi remained silent.
The NCP leader was addressing a discussion titled “One Year of the Verdict: Sheikh Hasina's Trial, Extradition and State Accountability”, arranged by the party’s July Mass Uprising Cell to mark the first anniversary of the death sentence against Sheikh Hasina for crimes against humanity during the July 2024 mass uprising.
He also accused India of applying double standards on cross-border security issues.
To explain his position, Hasnat presented a hypothetical example of Bangladesh providing shelter to an ULFA leader and allowing the individual to organise attacks and violent activities in India's Assam from Dhaka.
He questioned whether India would tolerate such activities if they were directed against its own territory, arguing that New Delhi was unwilling to accept a situation that it was allegedly allowing in Bangladesh's case.
The NCP leader further alleged that India had been providing training and shelter to people involved in cross-border violence over the past two and a half years.
He said Bangladesh respected international protocols and India's sovereignty but could not remain silent over activities that threatened its own sovereignty.
Hasnat called on the government to raise the issue with India and demand clarification over how it had allegedly become a “safe haven” for people involved in terrorism against Bangladesh.

item.title: Law minister: Pallabi child murder trial completed, Hadi case to follow
item.description:
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the trial of Sharif Osman Hadi's murder will be ensured, announcing that appeals in the Major Sinha, Biswajit and Abrar Fahad murder cases will begin hearing at the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court from next week.
He also said the trial in the rape and murder case of eight-year-old Pallabi girl had concluded, with the accused sentenced to death.
The minister made the remarks in a statement under Rule 300 during the seventh day of the fourth session of the 13th parliament on Tuesday.
Recalling the Pallabi girl case, Asaduzzaman said the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl in May had deeply shaken the nation.
He said the child was raped and murdered by her neighbour, Sohel Rana, on May 19. Police arrested Rana and his wife on the same day. A case was filed the following day, and the charge sheet was submitted to the court on May 24. After completing the legal proceedings, the court delivered its verdict on June 17, sentencing both accused to death.
The law minister said the appeal in the case was also disposed of in the shortest time in the country's judicial history for a death penalty case.
He acknowledged the roles of the prime minister, the home minister, the chief justice and other concerned authorities in ensuring a speedy trial. He also thanked the Attorney General's Office and all those involved in the process.
Asaduzzaman said the girl's father had initially been reluctant to file a case, fearing that his family would not get justice. The prime minister, home minister and law minister later visited the victim's home and assured the family of justice and support. "The government has worked to fulfil that promise," he said.
The minister said the government had pledged to uphold justice despite all obstacles since taking office.
Ensuring justice for those who had disappeared, lost their lives, been subjected to enforced disappearance or political persecution, or fallen victim to crimes against humanity over the past 16–17 years was the state's responsibility, he said.
He added that the government would take initiatives to begin trials of crimes against humanity in districts across the country. On Hadi's murder, Asaduzzaman said the government was giving the investigation and trial the highest priority and taking all necessary measures on behalf of the state.
He also announced that appeals in the Major Sinha, Biswajit and Abrar Fahad murder cases would be heard by the Appellate Division in phases from next week, describing the move as part of the government's commitment to ensuring justice.
Seeking cooperation from opposition lawmakers, the law minister said the government would continue its efforts to establish justice despite any obstacles.

item.title: Stop making citizens pay
Ishraque: Hasina’s return in December claims political propaganda
Workers block Dhaka-Mymensingh highway over wage demands
item.description:
Garment workers staged protests and blocked several points along the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in Gazipur on Tuesday, demanding higher wages.
The workers began marching from Bhabanipur in Gazipur Sadar upazila at around 12:15pm, targeting the gates of several garment factories along the highway. The protests prompted around 70 factories to suspend operations for the day.
The workers blocked the highway at several points, including Bagher Bazar, Memberbari, Shirirchala and Gargariya Masterbari in Sreepur, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Police intervened after receiving reports of the unrest, dispersing the protesters and using sound grenades to bring the situation under control. item.title: Portuguese princess visiting Bangladesh
item.description:
A prominent member of Portugal’s historic royal family, Infanta Maria Francisca, duchess of coimbra (Portuguese princess), is visiting Bangladesh from Monday to November 24.
As a member of the House of Braganza, she is actively involved in social, cultural and humanitarian initiatives in Portugal and across Europe.
The visit brings together three important connections - royal heritage, Fair Pay and Bangladesh’s tea - and will provide an international platform for the heritage and global potential of Sylhet Tea, said a media release.
She will join the official launch of Sylhet Tea, London Tea Exchange’s new tea collection featuring premium teas from Sylhet, Bangladesh. The event will be held on Wednesday.
On the last International Tea Day, Braganza Blend, from the Sylhet Tea collection, was presented as the Portuguese Royal Family’s official tea.
The launch in Bangladesh will mark the beginning of Sylhet Tea’s journey into the global market, highlighting the heritage and international potential of Sylhet’s tea.
She is particularly known for her public engagements and charitable activities. During her visit to Bangladesh, she will take part in a number of cultural, social and humanitarian engagements.
A key purpose of her visit is to support the Global Fair Pay Charter, an international initiative founded by Sir Sheikh Aliur Rahman OBE, group chairman of London Tea Exchange, which promotes fair and dignified pay for workers around the world.
The initiative has received support from the United Nations, the Commonwealth, C40 and other international organisations, with Bangladesh emerging as an important partner.
The princess is also accompanied by several Global Ambassadors for Fair Pay, including representatives associated with Portugal, China and Pakistan.
Their participation will bring together international voices in support of fair pay, social responsibility and international cooperation.

item.title: HC upholds Sohel Rana’s death sentence in Pallabi child rape, murder case
item.description:
The High Court has upheld the death sentence of Sohel Rana, one of two convicts sentenced to death by a trial court for the rape and murder of a seven-year-old girl in Pallabi, Mirpur, in the capital.
The verdict was delivered by a High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja. Proceedings began at 10:38am on Tuesday. The date for the verdict was set after hearings on the appeals and death references concluded on Monday.
According to case documents, the victim's father, who works at a private office in Banani, lived with his family in a rented flat in Pallabi. Sohel Rana and Swapna Khatun lived in another flat in the same building. The child was a second-grade student.
The child was raped and murdered on May 19. After the crime, Sohel Rana fled by cutting through the window grille of the room. Acting on information received through the national emergency service 999, police took Swapna Khatun into custody, while Sohel Rana was arrested near Fatullah Police Station in Narayanganj.
The victim's father filed a case at Pallabi Police Station. On May 21, Sohel Rana gave a confessional statement before a court under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Both accused were subsequently sent to prison.
On May 25, the investigating officer, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station, submitted a charge sheet against Sohel Rana and his wife, Swapna Khatun. The case was also referred to the tribunal for trial that day.
The trial formally began on June 1, when charges were framed against the two accused. The following day, 16 prosecution witnesses testified, completing the recording of witness statements in a single day. On June 3, the accused were examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
On June 7, Judge Masrur Salekin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Tribunal for the Prevention of Violence Against Children delivered the verdict.
The tribunal ordered that both accused be hanged by the neck until dead under Section 368 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Under Section 374, the death sentences were referred to the High Court Division for confirmation.
The tribunal also fined Sohel Rana Tk5 lakh and Swapna Khatun Tk2 lakh, ordering that the money be paid to the victim's legal heirs.
It further ordered that if the fines remained unpaid, the Collectorate office could attach and sell the accused's movable and immovable properties, with the proceeds going to the victim's legal heirs.
The verdict was delivered just 19 days after the murder.
Following the trial court's judgment, the death reference, containing the relevant case documents, was sent to the High Court. Both accused subsequently filed jail appeals.

item.title: Postponed RMG wage board meeting rescheduled for Nov 23
item.description:
The postponed third meeting of the Minimum Wage Board, formed to set a new wage structure for garment workers, will be held on November 23.
At the meeting, the owners' representatives will present their proposed minimum wage, according to a board notice issued on Tuesday.
The third meeting was originally scheduled for Monday, when the owners' side was expected to present its wage proposal. They were also prepared for the meeting. However, it was postponed at the last minute, citing unavoidable circumstances.
It was later learnt that the meeting was postponed because workers' representative Md Anwar Hossain had fallen ill.
At the board's second meeting on November 9, the workers' representatives submitted their wage proposal, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk32,000 for garment workers.
The owners' side, however, did not submit any proposal at the meeting and sought seven working days to prepare one. The board instead gave them four working days to submit their proposal.
Worker unrest has continued across the garment sector for the past two weeks over demands for higher wages. Workers at various factories have been leaving workplaces without working after marking their attendance. Protests and clashes with law enforcers have also been reported in several areas.
Amid the situation, the government formed the Minimum Wage Board on November 1 to revise garment workers' wages. The board held its first meeting on November 4, where it agreed to implement the new wage structure from next month.
However, despite ongoing discussions over workers' demands, unrest in the industrial zones has not completely subsided.
The unrest has disrupted production and export activities at garment factories. To manage the situation, many factory owners have been forced to shut down their facilities under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act, 2006.
A total of 104 factories were closed under this provision on Sunday, while the number rose to 132 on Monday.

item.title: Garment workers block roads as unrest returns to Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
The industrial zones in Savar and Ashulia turned tense again on Tuesday after remaining calm for two days, as workers staged protests, clashed with police and blocked roads at several locations over their demand for higher minimum wages.
Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse the protesters, disrupting traffic on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway and causing long tailbacks.
Around 9:30am, workers of Standard Group gathered on the road near Padma Mor in Hemayetpur, under Tetuljhora union in Savar, instead of entering their factory. They later attempted to block the road by dumping waste and setting it on fire.
When police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) members tried to clear the road, clashes broke out between the two sides. Workers threw bricks and stones at police, prompting law enforcers to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them.
The workers later scattered and took positions on different roads and in nearby alleys. Intermittent clashes continued in the area.
Meanwhile, workers entered several nearby factories but reportedly continued work stoppages inside.
In another incident, workers attempted to block roads in the Khejurbagan area of Ashulia after 8:30am. Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them.
Around 11am, workers from several garment factories blocked the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Rajfulbaria, Savar, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Sub-Inspector Ibn-e-Farhad of Savar Model Police Station said workers from several factories, had gathered on the highway. Police and BGB members were working to restore normal traffic, he added.
Ali Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Savar Highway Police Station, said workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in the Fulbaria area around 11am.
Asaduzzaman Noor, in-charge of Savar Highway Police Station, said traffic remained suspended as workers occupied the highway, causing long tailbacks on both sides. Police were working to restore normal traffic, he added.
Workers continued their blockade until 11:50am.
Eight factories in the industrial zone remained closed on Tuesday under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act, 2006.
Three others announced general holidays, while workers at five factories were observing work stoppages.
Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Saiful Islam said law enforcers dispersed workers who attempted to block roads in Ashulia.
He added that workers also tried to block the Hemayetpur-Keraniganj Road, prompting law enforcers to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to clear the road.
A total of 18 platoons of BGB have been deployed alongside police to maintain order in Savar and Ashulia, he said.
At around 11:15am, Savar Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ali Ahmed said protesters were still blocking the road. Dhaka district police, Industrial Police and highway police were jointly working to clear the road, and he expressed hope that the situation would be resolved soon.

item.title: 42 BGB platoons deployed in Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj
item.description:
A total of 42 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in industrial areas across Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and ensure public safety, according to BGB headquarters.
Of the deployed personnel, 20 platoons are in Dhaka, covering Mirpur, Savar, Hemayetpur and Ashulia, including areas near Yunus Convention Hall, Kathgara, Zirabo, Hameem Group, Midlar Group and Jamgara.
Another 15 platoons have been deployed in Gazipur, covering Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Mouchak, Konabari, Telirchala, Kashimpur, Bhogra Bypass, Gacha, Sataish and Salna.
The remaining seven platoons are stationed in Narayanganj, covering Shibu Market, Katherpul, Jalkuri, the BSCIC Industrial Estate, Chashara Mor, Kanchpur Bridge and Shimrail.
BGB headquarters is conducting continuous, technology-driven surveillance to monitor developments on the ground and coordinate operations, the force said.
The monitoring includes real-time footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other specialised equipment.
The BGB said it remains on high alert in coordination with the local administration and police to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and respond to any untoward incidents in the industrial zones.
The force added that it is maintaining constant surveillance and taking necessary measures as the situation evolves.

item.title: Crude bomb explodes at Mirpur Model Police Station
item.description:

However, Officer-in-Charge Hafizur Rahman said sound grenades had been deployed in response to a protest by garment workers, adding that the loud noise heard in the area was caused by the detonation of the grenades.

item.title: Police, BGB fire tear gas, sound grenades as Gazipur workers block roads
item.description:
Workers from several factories staged protests in Gazipur's Joydebpur and Chandana Chowrasta areas on Tuesday, demanding an increase in the minimum wage.
Their road blockades since the morning disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway, Joydebpur Road and Bhogra Bypass.
Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) members fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to bring the situation under control, triggering chases and counter-chases between workers and law enforcers
However, the workers refused to leave the roads despite the measures.
Workers also attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail Highway in the Naojor area over the same demand. Law enforcers later removed them from the road.
According to police and local sources, workers from several factories in Joydebpur and Chandana Chowrasta began protesting around 9am without joining their shifts. Hundreds of workers from different factories later gathered and took positions on the roads.
At one stage, they blocked the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway and Joydebpur Road, bringing traffic to a standstill.
Police and BGB members went to the scene and asked the workers to clear the roads. The situation soon escalated, leading to chases and counter-chases between the two sides.
Law enforcers later fired tear gas shells and sound grenades in an attempt to disperse the workers, but they continued their blockade.
Mohammad Amzad Hossain, superintendent of police of Gazipur Industrial Zone-2, said workers from several nearby factories had blocked the roads.
Law enforcers were working to remove them and restore normal traffic, he added.

item.title: Former DSCC mayor Sayeed Khokon arrested in Dhaka
item.description:

He was arrested around 7am on Tuesday.
According to a statement from the Special Response Battalion (SRB), a team of SRB-01 arrested him from House 13 on Road 9 in Baridhara.
Following his arrest, Sayeed Khokon was placed in the custody of Gulshan police station.

item.title: Nahid condemns attack on expatriate Bangladeshis, students in London
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam has accused activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, of attacking expatriate Bangladeshis and students from various universities after a reception held in London, saying several people were injured.
In a Facebook post on Tuesday, Nahid blamed what he described as “fugitive and extremist activists of the Awami League” for the attack and strongly condemned the incident.
In his post, Nahid said expatriate Bangladeshis from different parts of the UK, students from various universities, community leaders and leaders of the 11-party alliance attended the reception in London. He expressed deep gratitude and appreciation for their large turnout.
He alleged that after the event, fugitive activists of the Awami League attacked ordinary expatriate Bangladeshis and university students who had attended the program, leaving several people injured. He also wished the injured a speedy recovery.
Nahid said representatives of international human rights organisations and journalists from various media outlets were present at the event and witnessed the attack and violence firsthand. He expressed hope that the incident would draw international attention based on their firsthand accounts and collected information.
In his Facebook post, he said the people of Bangladesh had witnessed the Awami League's history of political violence, repression and destruction of democratic institutions.
He said individuals linked to the political force, which was ousted from power through the July uprising, were now attempting to suppress dissent through violence and intimidation even on foreign soil.
Such actions, he said, raised concerns not only about the safety of expatriate Bangladeshis but also about the democratic environment and political freedom.
“There is no right to use the opportunities of democracy to perpetrate anti-democratic violence,” he said.
Nahid added that using political asylum, freedom of expression and the right to assembly in a democratic country like the UK as tools for violence and intimidation was unacceptable.
He called on the UK government to ensure a prompt, impartial and effective investigation into the incident.
He also demanded legal action against those involved in the attack and effective measures to prevent acts of terrorism and violence carried out under the cover of the UK's democratic space.

item.title: Awami League, NCP activists clash in London, four injured
item.description:
At least four people were injured in clashes between activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned and the National Citizen Party (NCP) on a road behind London's Mayfair Hall following a reception for NCP Convener and opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam on Monday night.
The injured were admitted to local hospitals, while London police baton-charged protesters several times to bring the situation under control.
Members of the British-Bangladeshi community and prominent figures expressed strong dismay over the incident, saying that bringing political rivalries from Bangladesh to London was deeply embarrassing for the entire community.
The reception was organised at Mayfair Hall in central London by members of the British-Bangladeshi community as part of Nahid Islam's week-long visit to the UK.
During the event, activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations gathered outside the venue.
According to eyewitnesses and organisers, Awami League supporters threw eggs and water bottles at guests arriving at the event and confronted them outside the hall.
After the program ended, activists of the Awami League and the NCP engaged in chasing and counter-chasing, followed by around 20 minutes of scuffles on the road behind the hall.
Saiful Islam, Prothom Alo's UK correspondent who was present at the venue, said Nahid Islam entered Mayfair Hall at around 3pm, more than three hours ahead of the scheduled time. He was therefore able to enter before the protesters gathered.
Nahid avoided any direct confrontation as he left the venue through a back entrance instead of the main gate after the event.
The incident sparked strong reactions among British-Bangladeshi residents, civil society representatives and guests attending the programme.
Cultural organiser Mahbubur Rahman Shiblu said the long-standing culture of such disruptive behaviour must end so that community events abroad are not overshadowed by street violence.

item.title: Titumir: Every taka borrowed must deliver maximum economic, social benefits
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir today said the government is focusing not on how much it borrows, but on ensuring that every unit of public resources generates the maximum possible economic and social benefits.
"We are not debating whether we should borrow less or borrow more. Rather, our focus is on how to borrow better, invest better and ensure the highest economic and social returns from every unit of public resources, while remaining accountable to the people," he said.
He was speaking as the chief guest at the concluding session of the two-day 'International Debt Conference Bangladesh 2026' in Cox's Bazar.
Describing borrowing as a means rather than an end to development, Dr Titumir said borrowed funds should be invested in sectors that enhance productivity, improve infrastructure, create employment opportunities and develop human resources.
He stressed that the economic and social returns from borrowing must be commensurate with the liabilities passed on to future generations.
Highlighting the challenging economic circumstances facing Bangladesh, the adviser said geopolitical conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East had increased the country's energy import expenditure by $4.2 billion.
"This additional expenditure was neither our choice nor something we could avoid," he said.
Referring to the human impact of the economic pressures, he said around eight million Bangladeshis had fallen below the poverty line again amid inflation and economic disruptions.
Many people who had worked hard to escape poverty were pushed back into it, he said, adding that these were not merely figures in statistical records but real hardships affecting people's lives.
Dr Titumir said the figures were not intended to blame anyone but to explain the circumstances in which the present government began its journey.
Understanding the starting point, he added, was essential to properly assess progress and the challenges ahead.
Describing the country's debt situation, he said Bangladesh's public debt had exceeded Tk18.9 trillion, equivalent to around 36% of GDP. Total external debt of the public and private sectors stood at more than $104 billion.
The government was spending over Tk1 trillion annually on interest payments alone. In addition, he said, Tk 56,750 crore had previously been borrowed from Bangladesh Bank to finance the budget deficit.
Emphasising the need for prudent debt management, he said the government must take all existing liabilities and associated risks into account while formulating its borrowing strategy.
As grace periods on previously contracted external loans were coming to an end, debt repayment pressures would increase in the coming years, he noted.
Bangladesh repaid $4.49 billion in principal and interest on external loans in the fiscal year 2025-26, and the annual repayment amount could rise to $7.6 billion by FY2030, he said.
Therefore, he stressed, decisions on new borrowing must carefully consider interest rates, maturity periods, repayment schedules, currency composition and exchange-rate risks.
Identifying national ownership and credibility as two fundamental pillars of debt management, Dr Titumir said borrowing decisions must be aligned with the country's development priorities and economic realities.
Transparency regarding debt data, expenditure and risks, alongside accountability to the public, was directly linked to the credibility of government debt management, he added.
The adviser also identified increased revenue mobilisation as a key condition for sustainable debt management.
Noting that Bangladesh's tax-to-GDP ratio remained low, he said the government aimed to increase the revenue-to-GDP ratio by two percentage points over the next five years.
The target would be pursued through expanding the tax base, digitalising tax administration and bringing more economic activities into the formal sector, he said. Higher revenue collection would help maintain a balance between development expenditure and debt servicing.
Highlighting the government's initiatives, Dr Titumir said the present government had stopped borrowing from Bangladesh Bank to finance the budget deficit.
As a result, pressure on money supply had eased and inflation had started declining from around 10%. Foreign exchange reserves had also risen above $30 billion, he said.
He further said the interest rate on 91-day Treasury bills had declined from around 12% to nearly 8%. The government had also taken initiatives to mobilise financing through long-term bonds and Sukuk.
Emphasising the need to develop the domestic capital market as a source of long-term financing, he said Bangladesh must maintain a balanced mix of domestic and external borrowing, short-term and long-term financing, and concessional and market-based loans.
He also stressed the importance of exploring alternative financing mechanisms, including private investment, public-private partnerships (PPPs), blended finance and credit guarantees.
Regarding the use of new financial instruments, including sovereign Sukuk, the adviser said Bangladesh's local-currency government securities had been included in JP Morgan's GBI-EM index.
He described the inclusion as an important milestone for the country's domestic currency bond market.
Alongside strengthening the capacity of the domestic bond market for long-term financing, Bangladesh also had opportunities to raise funds from international capital markets in a responsible and sustainable manner, he added.
Dr Titumir underscored the need for institutional reforms in debt management, including the establishment of a dedicated debt management office, enactment of a Public Debt Act and strengthening analytical capacity for debt data and risk assessment.
Regular publication of debt information, a medium-term debt strategy, an annual borrowing plan and transparent disclosure of contingent liabilities arising from government guarantees would help identify fiscal risks in advance, he said.
Outlining the government's strategy for economic transformation, he identified three phases:
He said the country aimed to move forward through economic recovery, restoration of institutional capacity and structural reconstruction.
Referring to Bangladesh's aspiration to become a US$1 trillion economy by 2034, he identified production, industrialisation, export capacity and employment generation as the key drivers of economic transformation.
Highlighting the economic importance of social protection programmes, the adviser said initiatives such as the Family Card and Farmer Card would contribute to improving living standards, reducing poverty and expanding economic inclusion.
These programmes were not merely forms of assistance but strategic investments in human development and long-term economic capacity, he said.
He also noted that the World Bank and development partners viewed these initiatives as part of the government's planned and financially responsible strategy.
Dr Titumir said the success of debt management should not be measured merely by how much money a country borrowed or repaid.
Rather, the real measure of success would be the extent to which borrowed funds transformed the economy and people's lives and generated economic and social benefits for future generations, he added.
The two-day conference, held on November 15-16, discussed sustainable sovereign debt management, borrowing costs and risks, international bond markets, the IMF's debt sustainability assessment framework, development of domestic bond markets and alternative sources of financing.
Around 100 delegates from nearly 30 countries, including Bangladesh, participated in the conference jointly organised by the Finance Division and the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
Participants included officials from the Finance Ministry and Bangladesh Bank, debt management experts from different countries, and representatives of the World Bank, IMF and ADB.
Representatives from the debt management offices of Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Indonesia and Malaysia also attended the conference.

National University VC freed after 12-hour standoff; offices closed for three days
item.description:
National University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr ASM Amanullah was freed after being confined to his office for around 12 hours amid a protest by 988 reinstated staff members over their demands.
He was able to leave his office at around 11:30pm on Monday after the staff members staged a day-long siege and sit-in, pressing for resolution of issues related to seniority, promotions and outstanding salaries and allowances.
Meanwhile, the university authorities have decided to keep all university offices closed for three days, from Tuesday to Thursday, to address the situation.
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the university’s Syndicate on Monday night. It was announced in a press release signed by Taiyeba Tasneem Siraj, acting director of the National University’s Public Relations Department.
According to the release, all university offices will remain closed from November 17 to 19. However, essential services, the Office of the Controller of Examinations and activities related to the Principals' Conference will remain operational.
The 988 reinstated staff members had been protesting for the second consecutive day, demanding resolution of issues including seniority, promotions and payment of outstanding salaries and allowances.
They began surrounding the vice-chancellor’s office at the university’s main campus in Gazipur on Monday morning. At one point, they locked the main gate, effectively bringing the campus to a standstill and preventing the vice-chancellor from leaving his office.
The protesters said they had been reinstated following a court order but had continued to face discrimination over seniority, promotions and salary and allowance payments. They also alleged that they were being denied the benefits of the current pay scale.
They further claimed that while the university continued to recruit new staff and spend money in other areas, no effective steps had been taken to settle their outstanding dues.
On Sunday, the staff members had also surrounded the vice-chancellor’s office to submit a memorandum outlining their demands.
Amid the impasse, an emergency Syndicate meeting was convened at 10pm on Monday at the vice-chancellor’s office on the university’s main campus. The meeting was chaired by Professor Amanullah, and the decision to close university offices for three days was taken there.
In a Facebook post around 8pm on Monday, the vice-chancellor alleged that the 988 reinstated officers and employees had confined him for nine hours.
“My administration will not take any action that goes against the interests of the National University. I have acted in accordance with the court's verdict; for the rest, I will follow the government's directives. I have never bowed to pressure in the past, and I will not do so now,” he wrote.
He also said the university needed reform and that he had taken several initiatives towards that goal, but such efforts could not succeed if he was prevented from working.
Describing the blockade and confinement as futile, he wrote: “You have held me confined for nine hours; even if you were to keep me confined for 90 hours, it would achieve nothing.”
The officers and employees concerned were appointed to various positions between November 17, 2003, and August 31, 2004, but were dismissed from service in 2012, leading to a prolonged legal battle.
On May 27, 2025, a seven-member bench of the Appellate Division ordered the reinstatement of the surviving dismissed staff members. The court directed that their period of dismissal be treated as “extraordinary leave” and that their seniority be preserved.
However, the university authorities were tasked with determining matters relating to salaries, allowances and other benefits, taking humanitarian and practical considerations into account.
Following the implementation of the court verdict, the 988 reinstated staff members began protesting for recognition of their seniority, promotions and payment of outstanding salaries and allowances. The latest demonstration brought normal activities on the university’s main campus to a halt, prompting the authorities to call an emergency Syndicate meeting and announce the three-day office closure.

item.title: Holders India, first-time finalists Pakistan face off in SAFF final
item.description:
Defending champions India will take on first-time finalists Pakistan in the SAFF Championship 2026 final at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Tuesday.
India are aiming to secure a record-extending 10th title and become the first team to win three consecutive editions of the regional competition. Pakistan, meanwhile, will be looking to lift their maiden SAFF Championship trophy in their first-ever final appearance.
Scheduled to kick off at 8pm, the final promises to be a fascinating contest between the traditional rivals, with India seeking to extend their dominance and Pakistan hoping to script a historic triumph.
India are the most successful team in SAFF Championship history, having lifted the trophy in 1993, 1997, 1999, 2005, 2009, 2011, 2015, 2021 and 2023.
Despite their dominance, India have never won the championship in three consecutive editions. A victory on Tuesday would see them achieve that milestone while further extending their record.
Head coach Naushad Moosa's young side booked their place in the final with a 2-1 victory over Bhutan in the first semifinal. PV Vishnu and captain Chinglensana Singh Konsham scored in the first half to give India a two-goal cushion before Kinzang Tashi Tobden pulled one back shortly after the break.
Pakistan, meanwhile, made history by defeating hosts Bangladesh 1-0 in the other semifinal. Abdul Samad Arshad broke the deadlock with a late winner in the 86th minute to send Pakistan into their maiden SAFF final.
The victory marked another significant milestone in a remarkable year for Pakistan football, as they now stand just one win away from claiming their first regional title.
The traditional rivals have already met once in this edition, with India securing a 3-2 victory in their opening Group B encounter on November 5. India established a commanding 3-0 lead through a brace from Suhail Ahmad Bhat and a goal from Manglenthang Kipgen before Pakistan scored twice in stoppage time to make the contest considerably closer.
Pakistan's disciplined defensive display against Bangladesh, despite facing sustained pressure from the hosts, will provide them with confidence heading into the title-deciding encounter.

item.title: Ackerman leads South Africa fightback after Hasan strikes
item.description:
Marques Ackerman struck his maiden Test century to lead South Africa's fightback against Bangladesh, despite Hasan Mahmud's impressive bowling, as the hosts reached 287-4 at stumps on Day 2 of the first Test at the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg today.
Ackerman made 157 off 164, smashing 21 fours and one six while Zubayr Hamza scored 83, helping South Africa recover from an early setback and cut Bangladesh's first-innings lead to 113 runs. The hosts had resumed their reply after Bangladesh were bowled out for 400.
Captain Temba Bavuma was unbeaten on 19, with Ryan Rickelton on 7 at the close.
The highlight of South Africa's innings was a commanding 202-run second-wicket partnership between Ackerman and Hamza, who steadied the innings after Hasan removed Aiden Markram in the second over.
Markram, who made 5, tentatively edged a scrambled-seam delivery from Hasan.
Ackerman and Hamza weathered some testing spells, remaining unbeaten throughout the second session despite sustained pressure from Hasan and Taskin Ahmed.
Taskin came close to dismissing Hamza, who was trapped leg-before, but the bowler had overstepped and the delivery was called a no-ball.
Ackerman looked increasingly assured and brought up his third consecutive fifty off 68 balls, whipping Mehidy Hasan Miraz through deep midwicket for four.
Hamza, after some early struggles, also settled into his innings, reaching his half-century off 82 balls with a single off Mehidy.
With his frontline bowlers struggling to break the partnership, Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto turned to Mominul Haque, and the move paid off.
Mominul ended Hamza's resistance with his left-arm spin, dismissing him for 83 off 129 balls, an innings featuring 12 boundaries.
Ackerman continued to dominate, reaching his maiden Test century off 125 balls with a single off Taskin. He then accelerated, putting Bangladesh's bowlers under further pressure before Hasan ended his innings at 157, having him caught by Taskin at backward square leg.
The dismissal also broke a 61-run partnership between Ackerman and Bavuma. Hasan struck again soon afterwards, removing Matthew Breetzke for 2 to prevent South Africa from taking complete control of the contest.
He also could have dismissed Ryan Rickelton, who edged a delivery behind, but Liton Das dropped the catch.
Earlier, Bangladesh resumed the day at 327-6 but managed only 73 more runs before being bowled out for 400.
Liton Das, who began the day on 89, completed his eighth Test century off 154 balls, pulling Marco Jansen to the fine-leg boundary.
Dane Paterson eventually dismissed Liton for 120 off 154 balls, an innings featuring 14 fours and a six. He became the second Bangladesh batter to score a century in the innings, following Towhid Hridoy's 137.
It was the first time two Bangladesh batters had scored centuries in the same Test innings against South Africa. Their efforts propelled Bangladesh to 400, their highest Test total on South African soil.
Paterson then cleaned up the tail, taking all four remaining wickets in the morning session to finish with figures of 4-92.
